# 🆕 Trends new at `p765` (researched 2026-11-11) — `T627`–`T650`

**The register is school-estate safety and statutory compliance** — fire doors, asbestos, legionella, electrical fixed-wire testing and playground-equipment inspection. `ACTION p764-A` named it and this pass built it. It is a different buyer from `p764`'s condition register (risk and compliance, not capital planning) and a different cadence (dated statutory intervals, not bond cycles).

**`73` addresses probed for a grant · `61` licence payloads byte-read with length and `sha256₁₂` · `32` licence-family paths per address, now crossing the capitalisation of the **extension** as well as the stem · `16` language manifests on failure · `5` `COPYING.LESSER`-family paths whenever a GPL title line was seen · `15` agent READMEs fetched and counted at `125,076` bytes · `78` supply queries on `search/repositories` · `563` batched liveness calls and `377` individual re-probes across the whole base · every `default_branch` derived from the search channel, none guessed.**

## `T628` — 🔴 `INS-005`: on this register plain-language search does not return a noisy answer, it returns **another discipline**

`T592` and `INS-002` established that `in:name` is not a safe supply denominator. This register shows a harder case: three of its five statutory vocabulary terms are **homographs whose GitHub majority belongs to a different field entirely.** Measured on the top `30` by stars for each query:

| Query | `total_count` | What the top `30` actually are |
|---|---|---|
| `legionella` | `153` | **`24`** are *Legionella pneumophila* genomics, sequence-based typing and microbial ecology (`UPHL-BioNGS/Grandeur`, `tseemann/legsta`, four `CDCgov/*` pipelines, `phac-nml/legiovue`). **Exactly `1`** addresses the built-environment pathway — [`TowerScout/TowerScout`](https://github.com/TowerScout/TowerScout) at `21★`. The remainder include a heat-pump Modbus integration and an air-purifier spam page |
| `fire risk assessment` | `174` | **`22`** are wildfire and forest-fire modelling (`steidani/FireDanger`, `IAM-FIRE`, a dozen student wildfire-ML projects). The **top hit by stars is floor-plan computer vision** (`whchien/deep-floor-plan-recognition`, `81★`). **Exactly `1`** is building fire engineering — [`aamks/aamks`](https://github.com/aamks/aamks) at `23★` |

🔴 **The consequence is stated precisely: `153`, `174` and `46` are not supply figures for this register and must never be published as such.** A denominator is only a denominator once the discipline has been checked. 🔵 **This is `INS-002`'s class arriving through a different door**: there `in:name` tokenised a hyphen, here the English word is simply owned by another science.

## `T630` — 🔴 `INS-003` was right and still too narrow: capitalisation must cross the **extension**

`ACTION p764-B` widened the path set to cross capitalisation after Berkeley Lab's grant was found at `License.txt`. This pass built `32` paths on that instruction — and still missed a grant.

[`TowerScout/TowerScout`](https://github.com/TowerScout/TowerScout) (`21★`, index `NOASSERTION`) returned **no payload across `32` licence paths and `16` manifests**. Its grant is at **`LICENSE.TXT`** — uppercase *extension*, which was not in the set. `LICENSE.txt` returns `404` at the same address; `LICENSE.TXT` returns `200`, `20,843 B`, `5b8e7938e1b5`.

🔴 **And the verdict it was hiding is the one that matters: `CC BY-NC-SA 4.0` — NonCommercial.** The platform's index said `NOASSERTION`; the truth is a grant that forbids the delivery model. 🟢 **The recovery was free and should have been first**: the README's own `## License` section names the licence and links the file. **`ACTION p765-A`: when no payload is found, read the README's License section *before* publishing an absence.** One fetch, and this pass would not have needed a second pass over the same address.

## `T631` — 🔴 `T619`'s `COPYING.LESSER` rule paid out again, and this time it corrected **the platform's index**, not just a one-file read

`p764` raised `INS-004` on [`IfcOpenShell/IfcOpenShell`](https://github.com/IfcOpenShell/IfcOpenShell) and `ACTION p764-B` carried it forward: on a GPL payload, probe `COPYING.LESSER` before recording a verdict. It fired once this pass, on [`FireDynamics/fdsreader`](https://github.com/FireDynamics/fdsreader) (`79★`, branch `master`), the reader for Fire Dynamics Simulator output:

| Path | Bytes | `sha256₁₂` | Family |
|---|---|---|---|
| `LICENSE` | `35,131` | `8a4c9551082a` | GNU **General** Public License v3 |
| `LICENSE.LESSER` | `7,652` | `e3a994d82e64` | GNU **Lesser** General Public License v3 |

**GPL-3.0 plus a Lesser-permissions file is LGPL-3.0.**

🔴 **The advance on `T619` is in who was wrong.** `IfcOpenShell`'s own index reads `LGPL-3.0` correctly — only a one-file *reader* would have mis-graded it. **GitHub's index reports `fdsreader` as `GPL-3.0`.** So this is the first instance on this base where the two-file read corrects **the platform**, not merely a careless instrument, and the only check that catches it is the one `p764` wrote.

🟢 **It moves a row from refused to usable.** Under `GPL-3.0`, linking `fdsreader` into a proprietary deliverable infects the deliverable; under LGPL-3.0 it does not, provided the library stays replaceable. **The only fire-engineering data reader on this register changed verdict because one extra path was probed.** 🔵 `e3a994d82e64` is the same payload `T619` recorded on `IfcOpenShell`, so it was recognised the instant it was read — the defect was never in reading it, only in asking.

## `T635` — 🔴 `INS-006`: a `200` from `raw.githubusercontent.com` is not proof that an address is current

This is the defect that has let this base carry dead addresses for hundreds of passes, and it is two lines to state.

**`raw.githubusercontent.com` follows an organisation or repository rename silently. The search channel does not.** Measured on three addresses:

| Address as this base writes it | `repo:` on `search/repositories` | `raw.githubusercontent.com` | Current address |
|---|---|---|---|
| `openedx/edx-platform` | **`422`** | **`200`** (`master/README.rst`) | [`openedx/openedx-platform`](https://github.com/openedx/openedx-platform) `8,231★` |
| `snipe/snipe-it` | **`422`** | **`200`** (`master/LICENSE`) | [`grokability/snipe-it`](https://github.com/grokability/snipe-it) `15,168★` |
| `NVIDIA/NeMo-Guardrails` | **`422`** | **`200`** (`main/README.md`) | [`NVIDIA-NeMo/Guardrails`](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Guardrails) `7,474★` |

🔴 **Every verification this base has ever done by fetching a file would have scored all three green.** 🟢 **The working instrument is the one `p764` built**: `422` on `repo:<address>` plus a hit on `<name> in:name` or `org:<owner>`. **`ACTION p765-B`: liveness is a search-channel property; a payload fetch proves the bytes, never the address.**

## `T636` — 🔴 `ACTION p764-C` discharged across the whole base, and `p764`'s own figure corrected

`p764` asked for a scripted sweep for renamed organisations and estimated the exposure at *"`20` `NREL` mentions"*. Both halves needed correcting.

🟢 **First, a cheaper instrument.** Multiple `repo:` qualifiers in one `search/repositories` query are OR'd, and an absent address does **not** fail the batch — it is simply absent from the results. So liveness is a set-difference at **`10` addresses per call**, a tenth of the cost of `T621`'s per-address probe. `563` calls covered the base.

🟢 **Second, the census.** `5,621` distinct `github.com/<a>/<b>` addresses were extracted from the eleven shelves. **`50` were not repository addresses at all** — `topics/…`, `search/…`, `trending/…`, `repos/…` URL paths that the shape filter admitted, and all `50` were among the sweep's "missing", which is a defect in this pass's own instrument, found and removed before any number was published. Corrected denominator **`5,571`**:

| Class | Count | Share |
|---|---|---|
| `LIVE` — returned by `repo:` | **`5,194`** | `93.2 %` |
| absent or unindexed | **`377`** | `6.8 %` |

🔴 **Third, the response classes, which the batched form conflates and an individual re-probe separates.** All `377` were re-probed one at a time:

| Response | Count | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| **`422 Validation Failed`** | **`229`** | the address does not resolve on the search channel — renamed, deleted or made private |
| **`200` with `"total_count":0`** | **`148`** | the address resolves but the repository is **not in the search index** — it is *not* dead |

🔴 **Fourth, a units correction to `p764`, which wrote that this base "held `20` of them".** Measured three ways, that figure matches none: `NREL` appears as a **token** `387` times, as an **address** in exactly **`2`** distinct forms — `NREL/EnergyPlus` and the literal ellipsis `NREL/...` used in prose — and `NREL/EnergyPlus` carries **`10`** mentions. **There is one real dead `NREL` address on this base, not twenty.** `ACTION p765-D` is sized against `229`, not against a token count. And the real exposure is elsewhere: **`openedx/edx-platform` is `422` and is cited `49` times**, while this base *also* already carries the live successor `openedx/openedx-platform` `147` times. **It has known the new address all along and never retired the old one.** The `377` absent addresses carry **`1,246` mentions** in total.

🔵 **Resolved successors, each by `in:name` or `org:`:** `openedx/edx-platform` → `openedx/openedx-platform` (`8,231★`) · `microsoft/presidio` → [`data-privacy-stack/presidio`](https://github.com/data-privacy-stack/presidio) (`11,833★`) · `NVIDIA/NeMo-Guardrails` → [`NVIDIA-NeMo/Guardrails`](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Guardrails) (`7,474★`) · `UCL-INGI/INGInious` → [`INGInious/INGInious`](https://github.com/INGInious/INGInious) (`243★`) · `NSoiffer/MathCAT` → [`daisy/MathCAT`](https://github.com/daisy/MathCAT) (`131★`, moved to the DAISY Consortium) · `IMSGlobal/openbadges-validator-core` → [`1EdTech/openbadges-validator-core`](https://github.com/1EdTech/openbadges-validator-core) (`61★`; `org:IMSGlobal` now returns **`1`** repository against `org:1EdTech`'s `46`). 🔴 **`trilogy-group/oneroster-ts` has no establishable successor** — two same-named repositories exist at `0★` and neither is provably the same code; it is recorded as absent with the successor unresolved.

🔴 **One address resists both classes and is recorded as the anomaly it is:** `digitalcredentials/learner-credential-wallet` returns `422` on `repo:` while `learner-credential-wallet in:name` returns that exact `full_name` at `1★`, and `org:digitalcredentials` returns `92` repositories. The channel contradicts itself on one address. No story is offered.

## `T637` — 🔴 the standards bodies are this register's chokepoint, and three of them closed in different ways

Statutory compliance is a register where the code is cheap and **the law is the asset**. Measured across four standards bodies this pass:

| Body | Instrument | What this pass measured |
|---|---|---|
| **buildingSMART International** | IDS — Information Delivery Specification, the computer-interpretable XML standard for *requiring* information of a model | 🔵 **`T618`'s finding, re-read and reproduced exactly**: [`buildingSMART/IDS`](https://github.com/buildingSMART/IDS) `333★`, index `NOASSERTION`, branch `development`, grant **by reference** at `287 B` / `e0af6597dc57` — **`CC BY-ND 4.0`, NoDerivatives**. Same bytes, same sha, one pass later |
| **1EdTech** (formerly IMS Global) | Caliper analytics | `1EdTech/caliper-js` is **`422`** and cited `11` times here. A surviving third-party fork carries the notice: *"1EdTech will be moving Caliper to private repositories on June 1"*. **Withdrawn, not renamed** |
| **BSI** | BS 8214, the fire-door code of practice | A paid standard. 🔵 **Verification blocked**: `knowledge.bsigroup.com` is refused at this tunnel |
| **Saudi Building Code** | SBC 201-CC-2024 | [`Kaiiser-ai/sbc-mcp-server`](https://github.com/Kaiiser-ai/sbc-mcp-server) is MIT and states in its own README: *"The Saudi Building Code (SBC 201-CC-2024) content is **not included** in this repository due to copyright."* **Permissive server, absent corpus** |

🔴 **What this pass adds to `T618` is the scope line, because the obvious reading is wrong in both directions.** NoDerivatives means a *modified or extended IDS specification* may not be published — so a "Globant statutory-compliance IDS profile" presented as a derivative of the spec is refused, which is `T618`'s ministry warning. 🟢 **It does not restrict IDS *files***: an `.ids` document you author that conforms to the spec is your own work, not a derivative of the standard's text, and the statutory intervals of `T642` and `T645` are exactly what such a file would encode. **Implement against it, author your own, never republish it changed** — and the MIT reader this base already holds, [`vinnividivicci/ifc-ids-mcp`](https://github.com/vinnividivicci/ifc-ids-mcp), stays the right component.

🔴 **The genuinely new reading here is `1EdTech`.** `T618` found a standards body restricting its grant; this pass finds one **withdrawing its code from public view entirely**, with the notice preserved only on a third-party fork. A restricted grant can be worked around. A private repository cannot.

## `T639` — 🟢 the one architecture on this register with no vendor in the data path, and the copyright asymmetry that places it

Two MIT OSHA servers were read. They are the same idea and opposite deliverables.

| Repository | Grant | Where the regulation comes from | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`contextkits/osha-compliance-assistant`](https://github.com/contextkits/osha-compliance-assistant) `2★` | MIT, `1,068 B`, `9f2d6a2cf5be` | **A hosted API with an API key and published tiers: Sandbox `10` calls/day free, Developer `$79`/mo, Team `$199`/mo, Enterprise `$499`/mo** | 🔴 the MIT grant covers a **thin client**; the compliance knowledge is a metered subscription. `T584`'s vendor-portal class, in its sharpest form yet |
| [`dtjohnson83/osha-mcp`](https://github.com/dtjohnson83/osha-mcp) `1★` | MIT, declared in `package.json` (`1,542 B`, `80c18d157945`) | **`npx tsx scripts/ingest-standards.ts  # Fetch from eCFR`** into a self-hosted Supabase, covering `29 CFR 1910` and `1926`, with `5` tools including `get_standard_text` | 🟢 **no vendor anywhere in the data path** |

🔵 **The reason the second one can exist is jurisdictional, and it is the governing commercial fact of this register.** US federal regulation is a work of the United States government and carries no copyright, so the corpus can be ingested and redistributed. England's statutory content splits: HSE guidance is Crown copyright published under open terms, while the British Standards it points to (`BS 8214` for fire doors) are paid BSI products. Saudi Arabia's SBC is copyrighted and its own MIT server ships without it (`T637`).

🔴 **So the same agent is buildable in North America, half-buildable in England, and not buildable from open sources in the Gulf — and the code licence tells you none of that.** 🔵 **Verification blocked and labelled**: `www.ecfr.gov`, `www.hse.gov.uk`, `www.flsenate.gov` and `knowledge.bsigroup.com` are all refused at this session's tunnel. **Four primary verifications blocked; every statutory interval and figure on these shelves this pass is marked search-sourced.**

## `T640` — 🔴 a copy found by a single trailing space, and the third mechanism in three passes

[`lucksmiler-A1/Hazard-Image-Analysis-Agent`](https://github.com/lucksmiler-A1/Hazard-Image-Analysis-Agent) (`1★`, MIT, `1,080 B`, `50f4fa4a7be0`) is **a copy of [`buptlg/fireagent`](https://github.com/buptlg/fireagent)** (`77★`, MIT, `1,079 B`, `523f007cf103`). Its README describes "FireAgent", and its grant names the same holder — `Copyright (c) 2026 FireAgent contributors`. `diff` returns exactly one hunk:

```
3c3
< Copyright (c) 2026 FireAgent contributors
---
> Copyright (c) 2026 FireAgent contributors·
```

**One trailing space.** Recorded so the two are not counted as two agents.

🔵 **Three passes, three distinct one-character mechanisms that break a sha while preserving a grant**: `p761` a bracket-for-brace swap, `p763` a blank line added and a trailing newline stripped, `p765` a single trailing space. **Corollary, and it is the half `ACTION p762-A` never stated: sha *inequality* does not prove independence any more than sha equality proves identity.**

## `T641` — 🔴 there is no permissive statutory-compliance platform, and this is the third consecutive register to say so

`14` platform-tier systems were byte-read. **`13` are AGPL-3.0 or GPL-3.0.** The single permissive one, [`vtellier/OpenMaintenance`](https://github.com/vtellier/OpenMaintenance) (Apache-2.0, `11,357 B`, `c71d239df917`), has **`2★`**.

🔴 **And the vertical's own named platform is not on GitHub at all.** `openMAINT` is the facility-management vertical of CMDBuild and the obvious system of record here. Every `openmaint` address that resolves is a **third-party dockerisation** — `itmicus/cmdbuild_docker` (`125★`, no payload across `32` paths and `16` manifests), `rsilva4-zz/docker-openmaint` (`36★`, MIT **on the wrapper**), `chabala/docker-openmaint` (`10★`), `astmnk/docker-openmaint` (`2★`, archived), `bigdoods/openmaint` (`1★`, archived). **The platform is distributed off-platform and its grant cannot be read from here.**

🟢 **`p757`'s law holds for a third register running**: `p757` found the system of record copyleft, `p762` found *"there is no permissive HRIS"*, and `p765` finds there is no permissive statutory-compliance system either. **Three registers, no counter-example. This is now a prior, not an observation.**

## `T642` — EMEA: the statutory instrument is dated, the return is becoming digital, and the national register was refused

🟢 **England is the most precisely specified school-estate compliance regime this base has measured.** The duty sits on the employer — local authority, governing body or academy trust — under the Health and Safety at Work Act 1974, the Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations 1999, the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005 and the **Control of Asbestos Regulations 2012**. Asbestos: any school built or refurbished **before 2000 must be presumed to contain it** until a specialist proves otherwise, and a 2019 DfE survey is reported as finding **around four in five schools** do.

🟢 **The buyer's instrument now has a name and a date.** The DfE's second Condition Data Collection (**CDC2**) covers about **`22,000` school buildings**, added RAAC in 2021 and concludes in **2026**; responsibility for condition data moves to responsible bodies, with pilots in 2026–27 and national rollout from autumn 2027. **From autumn 2026 responsible bodies make an annual return through a new digital service, *Manage Your Education Estate*, confirming they meet the School Estate Management Standards.**

🔴 **And the decisive negative: a parliamentary committee recommended a national digital asbestos register for schools and the government rejected it in April 2026.** RAAC is reported as confirmed in around **`1 %`** of schools and colleges.

🔵 **What this means commercially**: the compliance *return* is being digitised centrally while the *evidence* behind it — the fire-door log, the asbestos register, the legionella sample — stays with thousands of responsible bodies and has no open system of record. 🔴 **All figures search-sourced; `www.hse.gov.uk` and the DfE primary pages are refused at this tunnel, and one consultancy source contradicts the CDC rollout timeline. Both readings are recorded; neither is adopted.**

## `T643` — APAC is the mandate region and a real supply region, measured

🟢 **India is the clearest mandate.** A Government Resolution dated **13 December 2025** makes the Ministry of Education's *Guidelines on School Safety and Security-2021* mandatory in one state, building on a 13 May 2025 resolution; directorate circulars in mid-2026 require schools to **physically audit themselves against the *Manual of Safety & Security in School* and report deficiencies**. In Tamil Nadu, proceedings of the Director of School Education dated **7 May 2026** direct every District Chief Education Officer to complete a school safety and infrastructure audit **before the June reopening**, benchmarked on the *School Child Safety Handbook 2024-2025*, with each district reporting back. For buildings: from the **2026-27** session CBSE made the state NOC optional, but a **fire safety certificate and a building safety certificate remain mandatory on the SARAS portal**; schools are Group B (Educational) occupancy under the National Building Code Part 4.

🟢 **APAC also supplies code on this register**, which is unusual: [`buptlg/fireagent`](https://github.com/buptlg/fireagent) (`77★`, MIT, China) is the highest-starred on-register agent anywhere; [`PerryLink/dsh-eia-guide-check`](https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-eia-guide-check) (Apache-2.0, `11,339 B`, `9dac4ebe34dc`) cross-checks environmental-assessment guideline references; [`AnuwatThisuka/cmms-mcp-server`](https://github.com/AnuwatThisuka/cmms-mcp-server) (MIT, Thailand) is an MES/CMMS MCP server; `Safety-Bin/ehs-system` (Korea) reviews statutory items and amendment impact but **publishes no grant**.

🔴 **`ACTION p763-D` fired again and is now a standing hazard, not an incident.** The mandated APAC search leg returned, inside an APAC result set, the **UAE's** February 2026 generative-AI school prohibitions and a **UK** standard. Both are EMEA in this base's closed vocabulary. Neither is filed under APAC. **`region` is never populated from a source's own regional framing.**

## `T645` — North America: the instrument is state-level and the artefact is a filed report

🟢 **Two states specify it precisely enough to build against.** New York's 2026 manual requires **every building owned, operated or leased by a public school district or BOCES** to be inspected for fire safety, with school officials filing the annual **Fire and Building Safety Report**. Florida Statute **1013.12** requires district fire safety inspections by persons certified by the Division of State Fire Marshal, reports to the local fire authority, and **the district certifying completion to the State Fire Marshal**. South Carolina's Office of School Facilities manual carries fire and smoke protection provisions effective **16 February 2026**.

🔵 **The shape of the deliverable follows from that: the output is not a dashboard, it is a filed statutory return with a named signatory and a deadline** — which is the same shape as England's *Manage Your Education Estate* annual return (`T642`). 🔴 **No federal school requirement for indoor air quality or lead in water surfaced in this pass's searches**, and the ASCE `$85B` deferred-maintenance figure circulating in vendor material is **not** adopted here; `p764`'s `$90B` *State of Our Schools* reading stands and is the one this base cites. 🔵 **All three state instruments search-sourced; `www.flsenate.gov` is refused at this tunnel.**

## `T646` — 🔴 five defects in this pass's own classifier, each caught by a payload whose answer was already known

The instrument this pass was asked to build was wrong five times before it was right, and every correction was forced by a control rather than noticed by inspection. It is recorded because the failure modes are general.

| # | Defect | How it was caught | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| `D1` | GPL-3.0 classified as **AGPL-3.0** | `aamks/aamks` and `opf/openproject` are independently known GPL-3.0. Canonical GPL-3.0 **names "GNU Affero General Public License" three times** in sec 13 and the how-to-apply note | Anchor the family on the **title line**; confirm with a discriminator (`Remote Network Interaction`: AGPL `1`, GPL `0`) |
| `D2` | LGPL-3.0 classified GPL-3.0; MPL-2.0 classified LGPL-3.0 | `LICENSE.LESSER` and `engine_web-ifc` have known families. LGPL **incorporates GPL by reference** and therefore contains its name and `Version 3` | A partial match may never outrank a full one; title line settles it |
| `D3` | **Every** copyleft payload flagged `NONCOMMERCIAL` | Canonical AGPL-3.0 flagged itself. Both GPL-3.0 and AGPL-3.0 contain the word `noncommercial` in their own sec 5 / sec 7 text | Read restriction and composite flags from the **tail only** — after the body's own `END OF TERMS AND CONDITIONS` |
| `D4` | **The one payload the classifier existed to catch was missed** | `geovisor-asbesto`: MIT has no `END OF TERMS AND CONDITIONS`, so the tail was empty; and the composite detector matched only an English `creativecommons.org` URL, while this grant names CC BY 4.0 **in Spanish prose** | Tail starts after the matched family's own last operative sentence; second grants matched **by name, across languages** |
| `D5` | `D4` regressed: `18` false composites against `3` true ones | Canonical AGPL-3.0 and GPL-3.0 flagged themselves — **every copyleft family names itself in its own appendix** | Explicit per-family self-name exclusion |

🟢 **Final state, verified against `23` controls**: `5` flags, all true — `TowerScout` NonCommercial, `buildingSMART/IDS` NoDerivatives, `geovisor-asbesto` MIT + CC BY 4.0, `uchit/mcp-regulated-ai-compliance` Apache-2.0 + CC BY 4.0, and `xeokit/xeokit-sdk` AGPL-3.0 + a bundled third-party notices block naming four MIT components and MPL-2.0 for `web-ifc`. **`0` false positives on canonical payloads.**

🔵 **`D4` is the one to carry forward.** An instrument built to catch a class can be blind to that class in the only form it actually occurs in — here, a second grant stated in prose in the project's own language. **`ACTION p765-C`: any text detector on these shelves must be tested against a non-English instance before it is trusted.**

## `T649` — 🔴 `p276` wrote `14` corrections into these shelves and **a markdown renderer discards every one of them**

Found by a control added to this pass's substitute gate, not by reading. **`14` data rows across `agents/trending.md` and `repos/trending.md` carry one cell more than their table's header.** A markdown renderer renders the header's worth of cells and **silently drops the rest**.

🔴 **In all `14`, the dropped cell is the correction.** It opens `🔴 **SUPERSEDED `p276`**`, `🟢 **CORROBORATED `p276`**` or `🔵 **REFINED `p276`**`. One of them reads *"SUPERSEDED `p276` — AND THE ADVICE WAS WRONG."* **`p276` appended its re-verification to rows in two-, three-, four- and five-column tables that had no column for it, so its entire correction run is invisible to anyone reading the rendered page.** The content is in the file and has never been on the page.

| Shelf | Rows | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| `agents/trending.md` | `8` | `3>2`, `4>3` ×2, `5>4` ×3, `6>5` ×2 |
| `repos/trending.md` | `6` | `4>3` ×2, `5>4` ×3, `6>5` |

🟢 **Every location is enumerated in `evidence/overwide-rows.2026-11-11-p765.tsv`** and the gate now fails only on **new** over-wide rows, so the debt is bounded rather than silently carried. 🟢 **The repair is additive and must not rewrite the corrections**: give each of those `14` tables the column its fourth, fifth or sixth cell already assumes. **`ACTION p765-G`.**

🔵 **The general lesson, which is why this is a `T` and not a footnote.** An append-only shelf protects the *text* of a correction and guarantees nothing about its *visibility*. `p276`'s work was done, written and lost in the same pass. **A correction that renders into nothing is indistinguishable from a correction never made**, and nothing in this base's gates could see it until a column-count check existed.

[`buildingSMART/IDS`](https://github.com/buildingSMART/IDS) (`333★`, indexed `NOASSERTION`) is **CC BY-ND 4.0** — `287 B` · `e0af6597dc57`. ### `T619` 🔴 `INS-004`: LGPL is a two-file read, and a one-file read returns the wrong licence

[`IfcOpenShell/IfcOpenShell`](https://github.com/IfcOpenShell/IfcOpenShell) (`2,949★`) carries `COPYING` = **GPL-3.0** full text (`32,473 B` · `1b3782ccad7b`). Read alone, that convicts the library the entire register stands on as GPL-3.0 — which would make every derived tool GPL. The repository also carries **`COPYING.LESSER`** (`7,652 B` · `e3a994d82e64`), and the pair is **LGPL-3.0**, which permits linking.

🔴 **Every LGPL project in open source has this shape**, because the LGPL is defined as a set of additional permissions on top of the GPL. A licence instrument that stops at the first payload it finds will mis-grade all of them in the most expensive possible direction. 🟢 **The rule: on finding a GPL payload, probe `COPYING.LESSER`, `COPYING.LIB` and `LICENSE.LESSER` before recording a verdict.**

## `T595` — the trailing-newline strip, and `p761`'s constants vindicated

🔴 **This pass's first-cut licence probe read every payload through `$(command substitution)`, which strips trailing newlines.** Every payload ending in `\n` was reported **one byte short, with a sha256 that no file on disk reproduces**. The defect produced three false readings before it was caught:

|---|---|---|
| `TimefoldAI/timefold-solver` | `11,357 B` · `58d1e17ffe51` | 🟢 **`11,358 B` · `cfc7749b96f6`** |
| `kimai/kimai` | `34,522 B` · `4df3c306ddda` | 🟢 **`34,523 B` · `0d96a4ff68ad`** |
| `TimefoldAI/timefold-quickstarts` | `11,356 B` · `43070e2d4e53` | 🟢 **`11,357 B` · `c71d239df917`** |

🟢 **The catch was `p761`'s own data.** The stripped read put timefold-solver at `11,357 B`, which contradicted `p761`'s published `11,358 B` · `cfc7749b96f6`. Measuring the file reproduced `p761` exactly. 🔵 **So `p761`'s constants are sound and this pass's first instrument was the defect** — and on the strength of the stripped reading this pass had very nearly published a false "AGPL second-preimage at `34,522 B`" (the two AGPL payloads are `34,522` and `34,523 B`; the difference is a trailing newline plus a byte-neutral rewrap of the "how to apply" boilerplate at lines `636`–`637`, and both are verbatim AGPL-3.0).

🟢 **`ACTION p762-D`: measure the file, never the command substitution.** A licence instrument that cannot reproduce a known constant is not reporting about the repository.

🔴 **`2 / 8` — `25%` — and both hits are among the largest repositories in the register** (`or-tools` `14.4k★`, `erpnext` `41.2k★`). That is the same distribution `p761` measured for its own false negatives, and the same explanation: large, long-lived projects are the ones with release branches, vendored notices and non-standard defaults.

🔵 **The correction to this base.** `p761` published or-tools as *"Apache-2.0 · `45,765 B` · `b1282fbc0b7a` (Apache text **plus bundled third-party notices** — read the tail before shipping a notices file)."* The bytes are real and the advice was sound for what it read, but **it is the `main` branch's payload, and `main` is not the default branch.** A studio vendoring or-tools from the default branch gets a plain `11,358 B` Apache grant and no bundled notices. 🟢 **Both readings are now on the shelves with their branch named, because which one governs depends on which branch is actually vendored** — and that, not the byte count, is the thing to record.

🟢 **`ACTION p762-B`: a licence row names the branch it was read from, and that branch is the default branch.** Where the API that returns `default_branch` is refused, read it from the rendered page and say so. **Re-read every row this base has published for repositories above ~`1,000★`**, because the measured disagreement rate on exactly those is `25%`.

## `T598` — 🔴 a README that says MIT over a grant that forbids selling a service

[`workforce-data-initiative/skills-ml`](https://github.com/workforce-data-initiative/skills-ml) (`178★`, default `master`) is the Open Skills Project's skills-extraction library — the natural component for mapping teacher qualifications onto a competency taxonomy. GitHub's sidebar names **no licence**. Its README states *"This project is licensed under the MIT License."* Its `LICENSE.md`, byte-read at `1,976 B`, sha256₁₂ `2cc582006b14`, is neither:

> Copyright ©2018. The University of Chicago. … Permission to use, copy, modify, and distribute this software … **for educational and not-for-profit research purposes**, without fee … **For the avoidance of doubt, educational and not-for-profit research purposes excludes any service or part of selling a service that uses the Program.** To obtain a commercial license … contact the Technology Commercialization and Licensing, Polsky Center for Entrepreneurship and Innovation, University of Chicago.

🔴 **The excluded activity is the delivery model.** A studio engagement is a service, and the grant excludes any service or part of a service. There is no permissive reading: a commercial licence must be negotiated with the Polsky Center or the component cannot be used.

🔴 **Second consecutive register in which the key component's grant forbids consulting delivery, by a different mechanism each time.** `p761` found `giziiq` — title line `MIT License`, `Commons Clause` withholding fees for hosting or consulting. `p762` finds `skills-ml` — README says MIT, bespoke university grant excluding services. 🔵 The band rule from `ACTION p761-A` caught this one on sight: `1,976 B` is nearly twice the measured MIT ceiling, and the first line is not a licence title at all.

🟢 **`ACTION p762-E`: no licence claim originating outside the `LICENSE` payload may be shelved** — not the index, not the title line, not the README, not an aggregator. All four were wrong about something this pass.

| `kimai/kimai` | `5.1k` | 🔴 AGPL-3.0 |
| `opencats/OpenCATS` | `781` | 🟠 **dual: MPL-2.0 + CATS Public License v1.1a** |

🔵 **`OpenCATS` is the only non-GPL-family record-holder in the register and it is not simply MPL.** Its `LICENSE.md` (`43,229 B`, sha256₁₂ `e012562b38ed`) opens *"This application is available under two licenses"*: the OpenCATS code under MPL-2.0, and **original 2007 'CATS Project' code under the CATS Public License v1.1a, a modified Mozilla Public License.** GitHub's sidebar names no licence for it — correctly, since no single SPDX identifier describes it. A studio can work with MPL-2.0's file-level copyleft; the bespoke 2007 limb needs reading before anything derived from that code ships.

🔴 **The commercial consequence, stated plainly:** there is no permissive HRIS. Every engagement in this register either accepts GPL obligations on the record layer, or keeps the record in the client's existing proprietary system and composes permissive components around it. The second shape is the only one that preserves a proprietary deliverable, and it is what `P305`–`P310` are built on.

## `T600` — the open-source resume agents are built for the applicant, not for the school district

Measured by stars, the employer side of this register is a rounding error against the candidate side:

🔵 **The reading that matters for a district.** The applicant side is tooled, permissively, at `29.2k` stars and growing; the HR office receiving those applications has one `7.3k★` MIT scoring pipeline whose own reception included disputed, inconsistent scores on independent validation. **The volume arriving at a district's inbox is being automated faster than the district's capacity to read it**, and that asymmetry — not a productivity story — is the engagement.

## `T601` — 🔴 the regulatory double-bind: this register is education AI *and* employment AI at once

`Annex III` appears **`586`** times across these eight shelves. Contexts pairing it with employment, recruitment, hiring or workers: **`1`**. 🔵 **The base has held the EU AI Act's education limb for hundreds of passes and never its employment limb — and a teacher-hiring system sits in both.**

Dated US instruments, all **search-sourced, not primary-verified** (`ACTION p758-B`'s blocker is carried: primary hosts refuse at this tunnel):

| Instrument | Status as read 2026-11-11 | What it requires |
|---|---|---|
| **NYC Local Law 144** | 🔴 **in force since `2023-07-05`** | Independent annual **bias audit** of an automated employment decision tool, **results published**, candidate notice. Penalties reported at `$500`–`$1,500` per day per violation. A NY State Comptroller audit of `2025-12` found the enforcing agency's enforcement ineffective |
| **Illinois HB 3773** | 🔴 effective `2026-01-01` | Amends the Illinois Human Rights Act; notification and transparency rather than audits; prohibits discriminatory outcomes **regardless of intent**. 🔵 One source says the rules were paused — unresolved, flagged rather than picked |
| **Colorado SB 26-189** | 🔵 signed `2026-05-14` | **Repealed and replaced the 2024 Colorado AI Act before it took effect**, removing bias-audit and risk-assessment duties; applies to decisions on or after `2027-01-01` |
| **California ADS regulations** | in force `2025-10-01` | Automated-decision rules reaching employment |
| **Texas TRAIGA** | effective `2026-01-01` | Responsible AI Governance Act |
| **Connecticut** | first hiring rule `2026-10-01` | — |
| **EU AI Act Annex III** | high-risk regime `2027-12-02` | Both the **education** limb and the **employment** limb; Digital Omnibus political agreement `2026-05-07` |

🟢 **The commercial reading is favourable and it is the opposite of a blocker.** A district deploying an AI screening tool in New York City owes a published independent bias audit *today*, not in 2027 — and the audit is a deliverable a studio can produce whether or not it built the tool. 🔴 **The trap is the inverse:** a studio that ships a teacher-screening model into NYC without an audit has put the client in breach of a law that has been enforceable for three years.

## `T602` — EMEA, and `ACTION p761-F` discharged at national level with a channel defect attached

`ACTION p761-F` said: stop running the EU-level query, probe **national** authorities. 🟢 **Done, and it returned an artefact and a defect.**

🟢 **Sweden's Arbetsförmedlingen** (the national public employment service) publishes the **JobTech Taxonomy** — the Swedish labour market's occupation and skills vocabulary, ESCO-compatible, ~`5,950` skills against ESCO's ~`13,890` (a forum count, not an official statistic), served as REST and GraphQL. Its documentation states the API is **EPL-2.0**. 🔴 **Its source is not on GitHub** — it is on the JobTechDev forge — so `JobtechDev/jobtech-taxonomy-api` returned no payload across `39` probe points. 🔵 **A GitHub-only licence probe reports a false absence for a national authority's artefact.** That is a channel limitation, not a supply nil, and it is exactly the error class `ACTION p761-D` part 4 was written to stop.

🟢 **`ACTION p762-H`: for a public-sector artefact, probe the authority's own forge before recording an absence.**

**OECD *Education at a Glance 2026* makes teacher shortages its special focus** — shortages affect most OECD systems, and an ageing workforce is named as the compounding pressure. Netherlands: **`2%`** of primary and secondary teachers in public institutions were not fully qualified in `2024/25`, against an OECD average of **`9.1%`** — and the Netherlands leads internationally on mid-career entrants (`zij-instromers`). 🔴 A widely-repeated figure of ~`40,000` unfilled German teacher posts was found only on an aggregator with no primary source and is **not** shelved.

## `T603` — APAC is the supply region for this register, stated precisely

🔵 **The open-source HRIS layer is overwhelmingly South and Southeast Asian in origin, and this is stated from sources rather than inferred from the code:**

- **OrangeHRM** — founded `2005` by Sujee Saparamadu; headquartered in Secaucus, New Jersey with its **R&D centre in Colombo**, Sri Lanka, and its CTO a University of Moratuwa graduate; MySQL co-founder David Axmark on the board. 🔵 **Not "Sri Lankan-authored" and not "American" — US-incorporated with Sri Lankan engineering.** Open-core: the free Starter edition gates external API access, payroll connectors and advanced recruitment behind a paid tier.
- **Frappe** (`erpnext`, `hrms`) — Indian, and `frappe/hrms` is the most complete free HR app in the register at `9.0k★`.
- **Horilla** — `1.5k★`, LGPL-2.1, default branch `2.0`; the page names no country, so none is asserted here beyond what it states: *"Made with ❤️ by the Horilla Team."*

🔴 **The licence consequence of that geography is the register's central constraint:** the region that supplies the record layer supplies it under GPL-3.0 and LGPL, and the region that supplies the *permissive* half is EMEA — `TimefoldAI`'s solver estate, Apache-2.0, built by the original OptaPlanner team which forked from OptaPlanner on `2023-04-20`. 🔵 **Permissive optimisation from EMEA, copyleft record-keeping from APAC, candidate-side agents from everywhere, and the employer side of a `70`–`80%`-of-budget function served by one MIT repository.**

## Actions adopted at `p762`

**`ACTION p762-A`** — supersedes `ACTION p761-B`. Never key a licence identity on a byte count, **in any family**. Measured this pass: six distinct Apache-2.0 byte counts, two distinct payloads at `11,357 B`, and two distinct MIT payloads at `1,065 B` (`T596`).

**`ACTION p762-B`** — a licence row names the branch it was read from, and that branch is the **default** branch. Where `api.github.com` is refused, take `default_branch` from the rendered page and label the read page-sourced. **Re-read every published row above ~`1,000★`**: the measured disagreement rate between default and guessed branch is `2 / 8` = `25%`, and both hits were the largest repositories in the batch (`T597`).

**`ACTION p762-C`** — vocabulary censuses are counted with **word boundaries**. Any published mention count taken with a bare substring grep is of unknown value until re-counted; this pass's own first census was off by `531` on one term (`T594`).

**`ACTION p762-D`** — measure the file, never the command substitution. A probe that reads payloads through `$(...)` silently strips trailing newlines and reports hashes no file reproduces (`T595`).

**`ACTION p762-E`** — no licence claim originating outside the `LICENSE` payload may be shelved: not the index, not the title line, not the README, not an aggregator. All four were wrong about something this pass (`T598`, `T600`).

**`ACTION p762-F`** — carry `ACTION p760-A`/`p761-G` unchanged. Two consecutive discharges, each finding a buyer larger than the register before it (`T593`).

**`ACTION p762-G`** — discharges `ACTION p761-H`. The `P###` namespace is hereby **reserved for compose patterns**, which hold the longer unbroken run and are the client-facing sequence; instrument findings take the prefix **`INS-###`** from this pass forward. Existing instrument-`P` tokens in `README.md` and the trending files are not rewritten — they are legacy and are to be read with their file.

**`ACTION p762-H`** — for a public-sector artefact, probe the issuing authority's own forge before recording an absence. A GitHub-only probe reported a false nil on Sweden's national employment service (`T602`).

**`ACTION p762-I`** — the EMEA leg returned a national-level artefact but **no European school-HR software buyer**: no budget line, no programme, no municipal procurement. Next pass should probe **school-staffing agencies and supply-teacher intermediaries** in the UK and Netherlands, which are the commercial layer where that spend actually sits.


# 🆕 Trends new at `p761` (researched 2026-11-11) — `T583`–`T592`

**The register is student transport and school feeding — the two largest operational line items in a school system's budget.** The governing finding is about this base rather than about a market, for the second consecutive pass and in the same shape: the solver substrate that is the entire technical content of both halves has been on these shelves for hundreds of passes under the name *timetabling*, while the buyers whose procurement is defined by it appeared `1` and `0` times. `ACTION p760-A` was adopted last pass as a rule and this is its first discharge.

**A note on form, stated once.** This section is written in plain declarative prose with the same structural conventions the shelves use — pass id, byte-read licence cells, region placement, `T` tokens, `ACTION` tokens. The emphasis conventions are used where they carry information (🔴 a refusal or a defect, 🟢 a usable finding, 🔵 a reading or a reclassification) and not as a register of voice. Nothing about the measurement discipline changes.

## `T583` — the substrate/buyer seam, stated as a law

A technical substrate shelved under the property it satisfies will not be found by anyone searching for the buyer whose procurement is defined by that property. Measured on these eight shelves before this pass: `OR-Tools` `36` mentions, `Timefold` `30`, `optaplanner` `11`, `valhalla` `10`, `OSRM` `9`, `VROOM` `6` — against `school bus` `1`, `vehicle routing` `2`, `school meal` `2`, `school feeding` `0`, `WFP` `0`, `PNAE` `0`, `cold chain` `0`.

The buyers so missed: a US school-district transportation department with `~21,000` unfilled driver posts and routing software as its **top** technology spending line, and the national school-feeding programmes that spent **`US$84` billion** of government money in 2024 reaching **`466` million** children across **`107`** countries. 🔵 **The seam is not an absence of research. It is an index built on the wrong key**, and `ACTION p760-A` is the correct repair — this pass confirms it works on the first register it was pointed at.

## `T584` — the vendor-portal MCP server as an evidence class

[`chrischall/alphaportal-mcp`](https://github.com/chrischall/alphaportal-mcp) is the only purpose-built school-transport agent on GitHub (`school bus MCP server` → `total_count=2`, and the other hit is unrelated). It is `0★`, carries **no grant at `81` probed paths**, was pushed `2026-11-10`, and states *"Developed and maintained by AI."* It wraps **AlphaPortal / AlphaRoute**, a proprietary parent-guardian portal, naming **Charlotte-Mecklenburg Schools** in its own README.

🔵 **The generalisation, and it is now the second instance:** an unlicensed one-person MCP wrapper over a vendor portal is **evidence about the data path**, not a component. `p760` filed `monarch-studentaid-sync` the same way and read the same conclusion — the institution's portal has a reachable private API and no public one. **When the only agent for a register is such a wrapper, the register's integration risk is vendor data ownership, and that belongs in the proposal's risk section before anything is built.**

## `T585` — a licence whose title says `MIT` and whose first clause forbids the delivery model

[`satryayogapratama-ux/giziiq`](https://github.com/satryayogapratama-ux/giziiq) — AI menu generation for Indonesia's MBG programme, the register's only APAC artefact — is indexed `NOASSERTION` and byte-reads `2,219 B`, sha256₁₂ `fb74fe065a59`. Its grep-detectable title line is `MIT License`. It states `License: MIT` in plain text. **And its first 18 lines are `Commons Clause License Condition v1.0`**, which withholds the right to *Sell*, defined to include *"fees for hosting or consulting/support services related to the Software."*

🔴 **The withheld right is a systems integrator's business model, named in the licence.** A studio that deploys and supports this for a ministry performs exactly the withheld act.

🟢 **`ACTION p761-A` — the detector is the byte count, not the title line.** The `11` MIT payloads byte-read this pass measure `1,057`–`1,099 B`. `2,219 B` is more than twice that ceiling. **An `MIT` title line on a payload outside the measured MIT band must be read in full before the row is shelved.** 🔵 This is the mirror of `p757`'s `T526` — asreview's Apache payload opens with `All rights reserved.` and the real grant starts on line 3, i.e. a title line too *pessimistic*; here the title line is too *optimistic*; and a single classifier reading first lines is fooled by both. **Read the whole payload or read the size; reading the first line is strictly worse than either.**

## `T586` — a star count is not an ingestion licence, and a content repository is not a code repository

[`TapXWorld/ChinaTextbook`](https://github.com/TapXWorld/ChinaTextbook) was returned by the mandated trending leg as a trending education repository: **`84,351★`**, pushed `2026-10-26`, **no grant at `81` probed paths**. It is a corpus of school and university textbook PDFs. 🔴 **The missing grant is not a software question — it is a copyright question about the textbooks themselves**, and the repository's popularity says nothing about whether the underlying works may be redistributed or used as training data. Not shelved. 🔵 **Recorded so the next pass does not propose it and so no engagement cites the star count as a reason to ingest it.**

## `T587` — a `200` is not a grant: the pointer payload

[`valhalla/valhalla`](https://github.com/valhalla/valhalla) (`6,439★`, index `NOASSERTION`) serves `master/LICENSE.md` with a `200`. The payload is **`44` bytes**: `For license information see [here](COPYING)`. Every existence probe and every licence probe this base runs terminates successfully on a file that grants nothing; a size-banding gate classifies `44 B` as *no known licence*. The actual grant is **MIT** at `master/COPYING` — `1,135 B`, sha256₁₂ `8bdb14aebb00`, three stacked holders (Valhalla contributors 2018, Mapillary AB, Mapzen). 🟢 **Any payload under ~`200 B` is a pointer to be followed, not a verdict to be published.**

## `T588` — `NOASSERTION` on byte-identical bytes, with every obvious explanation excluded

[`getodk/collect`](https://github.com/getodk/collect) is indexed `NOASSERTION`; [`getodk/central`](https://github.com/getodk/central) is indexed `Apache-2.0`. Measured: same organisation; `default_branch` = `master` on both; the only licence-shaped file at root on either is `LICENSE.md` (`LICENSE`, `NOTICE` and `COPYING` all `404` on both); the payloads are **byte-identical** at `10,494 B`, sha256₁₂ `d1ee81266b96`; neither is a fork.

🔴 **Same org, same branch, same filename, same bytes — two different index verdicts.** The cause was not determined and is not guessed at here. 🟢 **`ACTION p761-C`: `NOASSERTION` is a statement about the index and never about the repository, and no pass may publish it as a licence state.** 🔵 The sharpness of this instance is what makes it worth a token: this base has corrected `NOASSERTION` toward a knowable grant dozens of times, and `T588` shows the index can be wrong **while being right about the identical bytes in the next repository of the same organisation.**

## `T589` — this base's honest-negative class is biased against the repositories a client names first

This pass's licence script probed `8` filenames × `3` branches = `81` paths per address and returned `10` verdicts of `ALIVE-NO-GRANT`. Its own follow-up refuted **two**:

| Repo | ★ | Truth | The miss |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`Project-OSRM/osrm-backend`](https://github.com/Project-OSRM/osrm-backend) | `8,209` | BSD-2-Clause, `1,297 B`, `df207517bc08` | the path set carried `LICENSE.txt` but not **`LICENSE.TXT`** |
| [`frappe/erpnext`](https://github.com/frappe/erpnext) | **`41,172`** | GPL-3.0, `35,149 B`, `3972dc9744f6` | **`develop/license.txt`** — lowercase name **and** a branch that is neither `main` nor `master` |

🔴 **`20%` false-negative rate on this batch, and not randomly distributed: both false verdicts landed on the two highest-starred repositories in the `NO-PAYLOAD` set.** Large, long-lived projects are precisely the ones with idiosyncratic licence filenames and non-standard default branches. 🟢 **`ACTION p761-D`:** add `LICENSE.TXT`, `LICENCE.TXT`, `license.txt`, `license.md`, `COPYING`, `COPYING.md` to the path set; **derive the branch from `default_branch`, which `search/repositories` returns on every item** (this pass read it to settle `T588` and could have read it for every row); follow payloads under `200 B` as pointers; and **re-probe the accumulated `T302` honest negatives above ~`1,000★`** — a published licence absence on a large repository is now a measured-unreliable claim.

## `T590` — the canonical Apache-2.0 constant is not unique at its byte count

These shelves have published for hundreds of passes that a canonical Apache-2.0 payload is `11,357 B` with sha256₁₂ `c71d239df917`. Re-fetched this pass, [`assafelovic/gpt-researcher`](https://github.com/assafelovic/gpt-researcher)`/master/LICENSE` reproduces exactly that. [`wfp/designsystem`](https://github.com/wfp/designsystem)`/master/LICENSE` is **also `11,357 B`** and hashes **`b40930bbcf80`**. `diff` is **two lines**, both inside the APPENDIX boilerplate instructions: `"[]"` vs `"{}"`, and `Copyright [yyyy] [name of copyright owner]` vs `Copyright {yyyy} {name of copyright owner}`. Both are verbatim Apache License 2.0; the `{}` form is the older-formatting distribution of the identical text, and bracket-for-brace is a one-for-one substitution, so the byte count is unchanged.

🔴 **Any gate that treats `11,357 B` as implying `c71d239df917`, or that refuses a payload because its hash is not the recorded constant, falsely refuses a verbatim Apache-2.0 grant.** 🟢 **`ACTION p761-B`: record two canonical Apache families — `[]` → `c71d239df917`, `{}` → `b40930bbcf80` — and never treat a size match as a hash match.** 🔵 The wider reading: Apache payloads byte-read this pass measure `10,494` / `11,356` / `11,357` (two distinct hashes) / `11,358` / `11,359` / `11,408` / `45,765 B` across seven projects, every one genuinely Apache-2.0. **The byte count is a triage signal. It was never an identity, and this is the first second-preimage-at-equal-size these shelves have measured.**

## `T591` — the multilateral layer seam: presentation open, programme closed

The `wfp` GitHub organisation publishes **`9`** repositories and **`0`** of them is school feeding. `wfp/designsystem` — the UI kit — is Apache-2.0 (`233★`, cold `2024-04-12`); the live on-mission repositories (`surveydesigner`, `common-identifier-application` and two siblings) are **AGPL-3.0**. **School Connect**, WFP's school-feeding management platform deployed across all `500+` WFP programme schools in Burundi with pilots in Niger and South Sudan, is not on GitHub at all.

🔵 **Second independent confirmation of `p760`'s UNHCR / Education Cannot Wait finding** (`25` repositories between them, `0` education code). **Stated as a law: a multilateral agency open-sources its presentation and identity layers and keeps its programme system closed.** The operational consequence is specific — **plan every national-programme engagement as a build or a procurement, never as a fork** — and it is now supported by two agencies in two sectors, which is why it is a law here and was a single observation last pass.

## `T592` — `total_count` on a plain-language query is not a supply denominator

[`danderfer/Comp_Sci_Sem_2`](https://github.com/danderfer/Comp_Sci_Sem_2) — `223★`, no grant, cold since `2023-04-03`, description is the Bee Movie script — was returned as the **`#1` star-ranked result for three unrelated register queries in this one pass**: `school bus routing`, `school feeding`, and `school cafeteria point of sale`. On the last, **`7` of the top `10`** results are copies of the same viral text.

🔴 **Consequence: the `total_count` of a plain-language multi-word query measures keyword collision, not supply.** `school feeding` reports `total_count=348`; the on-register count in its top `12` by stars is `3`. 🟢 **`ACTION p761-E`: no pass may publish a `total_count` from a plain-language multi-word query as a measurement of supply.** 🔴 **This has retrospective force** — these shelves carry published denominators of exactly that provenance, and they are now of unknown value until re-measured with constrained queries (topic, language and path qualifiers) rather than prose.

**`ACTION p761-A`** — an `MIT` title line on a payload outside the measured MIT byte band (`1,057`–`1,099 B` across `11` payloads this pass) must be read in full before the row is shelved. `giziiq` passes a title-line classifier and forbids consulting fees (`T585`).

**`ACTION p761-B`** — record **two** canonical Apache-2.0 families, `[]` → `c71d239df917` and `{}` → `b40930bbcf80`, both `11,357 B`. Never treat a size match as a hash match, and never refuse a payload for failing to equal the recorded constant (`T590`).

**`ACTION p761-C`** — `NOASSERTION` may not be published as a licence state. It is a statement about the index, and `T588` shows the index contradicting itself on byte-identical payloads in one organisation.

**`ACTION p761-D`** — repair the licence probe in four parts: (1) add `LICENSE.TXT`, `LICENCE.TXT`, `license.txt`, `license.md`, `COPYING`, `COPYING.md`; (2) **derive the branch from `default_branch`** rather than guessing `{main, master, develop}`; (3) follow any payload under `200 B` as a pointer (`T587`); (4) **re-probe the accumulated `T302` honest negatives above ~`1,000★`**, because the measured false-negative rate on this batch was `20%` and both misses were the largest repositories in it (`T589`).

**`ACTION p761-E`** — no `total_count` from a plain-language multi-word query may be published as supply. Re-measure the existing published denominators with constrained queries (`T592`).

**`ACTION p761-F`** — the EMEA leg returned a **sourced nil** on European school-transport and school-operations digitalisation: no budget line, no programme, no vendor, no repository. Do not re-run the EU-level query next pass; probe **national and municipal transport authorities** instead (the Nordics and the Netherlands organise school transport municipally, so the buyer is a municipality, not a ministry).

**`ACTION p761-G`** — carry `ACTION p760-A` unchanged and keep running it. Its first discharge, this pass, found a sector with `US$84` billion of annual government spending at `0` mentions on eight shelves. It is the highest-yield rule currently on this base.

**`ACTION p761-H`** — a naming collision this pass declined to fix and must not leave unrecorded: the `P###` token namespace is used **twice** on these shelves — for compose patterns (`P295`–`P298` at `p760`) and for instrument findings (`P950`, `P977`, `P1065` in `README.md` and the trending files). The two sequences overlap and a reference like `P742` is ambiguous without its file. Next pass should rename one of the two namespaces; this pass continued the pattern sequence at `P299`–`P304` and used no instrument-`P` tokens at all.


# 🆕 Trends new at `p760` (researched 2026-11-11) — `T566`–`T582`

**THE REGISTER IS *EDUCATION IN EMERGENCIES* — CRISIS-AFFECTED AND DISPLACED LEARNERS — AND THE PASS'S GOVERNING FINDING IS ABOUT THIS BASE, NOT ABOUT A REPOSITORY: IT HAS HELD THE ANSWER FOR HUNDREDS OF PASSES AND HAS NEVER HELD THE QUESTION.** `Kolibri` appears `574` times across these eight shelves and `offline-first` `182` times, while **`education in emergencies` appears `0` times, `UNHCR` `0`, `Education Cannot Wait` `0` and `internally displaced` `0`.** 🔴 **The supply side is a measured nil in the register's own vocabulary and the demand side is the largest this base has sourced — `258` million children across `87` countries.** 🔴 **And the licence shape is the finding a proposal turns on: every offline content-delivery component on earth is `GPL` or `AGPL` except one organisation's three repositories, which are `MIT`.**

Measured across `agents/top.md`, `agents/trending.md`, `repos/foundations.md`, `repos/trending.md`, `verticals/solutions.md`, `intel/market.md`, `intel/trends.md` and `compose/patterns.md` at `p759` `HEAD`:

| `Kolibri` | 🟢 `574` |
| `offline-first` | 🟢 `182` |
| `Kiwix` | 🟢 `65` |
| `RACHEL` | 🟢 `46` |
| `education in emergencies` | 🔴 **`0`** |
| `UNHCR` | 🔴 **`0`** |
| `Education Cannot Wait` | 🔴 **`0`** |
| `internally displaced` | 🔴 **`0`** |

🔵 **This is a shelving failure, not a research failure.** The components were filed under the *technical* constraint they satisfy — low connectivity — and never under the *buyer* who has that constraint most acutely and has a dedicated multilateral fund to pay for it. 🟢 **Rule adopted as `ACTION p760-A`:** *when a substrate is held under a technical property, probe once for the institutional buyer whose procurement is defined by that property.* A sector with a named global fund and no mentions on eight shelves is a shelving defect.

### 🔴 `T567` — measured supply nil in the register's own vocabulary, declared with the queries that produced it

# 🆕 Trends new at `p759` (researched 2026-11-11) — `T547`–`T565`

**THE PASS'S GOVERNING FINDING IS A FALSIFICATION OF THIS BASE'S OWN PUBLISHED CONCLUSION.** For eleven passes this base held that the student-wellbeing and safeguarding register had **no open supply** — `p750` measured it and wrote *"measured supply nil for this region's named demand"* (`T429`), and `p748` parked the register as a candidate it would not build (`748-E`). 🔴 **Both were artefacts of the words used to search, not of the supply.** Probed in the *profession's* vocabulary rather than the sector's, the register yields **`8` permissively-licensed reasoning addresses, `6` of them at `0` mentions on this base before today**, plus `3` production platforms. The register is **buildable**, and `748-E`'s EMEA blocker dissolves on a reading of the prohibition that `748-E` never checked.

### 🔴 `T547` — the "measured supply nil" on this register was a vocabulary artefact, and this base published it twice

`p750` priced the North America demand side of this register in detail — PPRA written parental consent, the ISBE enforcement letter, the Gaggle/GoGuardian litigation front — and then concluded the supply side was empty, on these measurements: `student retention agent llm` → **`0`** repositories, `school safety llm agent` → **`2`**, and *"the entire open early-warning tier is `7 / 7` at `0★`"*. `p748` independently parked the register at `748-E` on a similar reading: `school counseling software` → **`0`**, `student mental health agent llm` → **`1`**, `wellbeing chatbot education` → **`4`**.

🟢 **Both measurements reproduce.** This pass ran the education-sector vocabulary and got the same thing: every address returned by `open source safeguarding school student risk early warning system github` is a single-author project on synthetic data, and the search channel's own summary of them was *"none is a mature, production-ready safeguarding platform… none of the results address child protection or safeguarding."*

🔴 **The nil was in the query.** The people who do this work are not called "student wellbeing engineers" — they are **counsellors, child-protection caseworkers and helpline operators**, and their software is indexed under their words. Probed as *psychological counselling*, *crisis/suicide risk assessment* and *child-protection case management*, the same register returns:

| Vocabulary probed | Reasoning addresses found | Permissive | Novel to this base |
|---|---|---|---|
| education-sector (`student wellbeing`, `early warning`, `school safety`) | `9` | `3` usable | `0` |
| clinical / helpline (`psychological counselling`, `suicide risk assessment`, `child protection case management`) | `10` | `6` | `6` |

🔵 **The generalisation, and it is this pass's rule.** *Before declaring a register supply-nil, probe the vocabulary of the profession that performs the work, not the vocabulary of the sector that buys it.* The sector names the **buyer**; the profession names the **repository**. `p693` found the same shape from the other direction — *"the channel two passes called empty produced `9` novel rows once the probe asked for a product"* — and this is its second confirmation on a different axis. `ACTION p759-A`.

### 🟢 `T548` — `748-E`'s blocker dissolves, and the mechanism is a reading of Article 5(1)(f) that `748-E` never checked

`748-E` parked this register with a sharp and correct-sounding reason: *"under the EU AI Act, emotion recognition in educational institutions is a **prohibited** practice, not a high-risk one — so an emotion-inferring wellbeing product is unsellable in EMEA rather than merely regulated."* 🟢 **The prohibition is real and the parking was wrong**, because the prohibition is narrower than the register.

🟢 **The European Commission's (non-binding) Guidelines read Article 5(1)(f) as limited to inference from *biometric* data**, consistent with the definition at **Article 3(39)** — even though the text of 5(1)(f) does not itself repeat the biometric qualifier. The worked examples that circulate with that reading are unusually concrete: inferring a student's **interest or attention** is prohibited; emotion recognition **during admission tests** is prohibited; **eye tracking in online exams is permitted only if it infers no emotions**.

🔵 **So the line that decides whether this register is sellable in EMEA is an *input* line, not a use-case line:**

| Architecture | Article 5(1)(f) |
|---|---|
| 🔴 Camera, microphone or physiological signal used to infer attention, engagement, mood or stress | **Prohibited.** No conformity assessment rescues it; it is not a high-risk system, it is a banned one. |
| 🟢 Classification of **text a person chose to write** — a disclosure, a help-request, a counselling transcript | **Outside the prohibition** on the Commission's biometric reading. Falls to be assessed under the high-risk regime and the GDPR, both of which are satisfiable. |

🟢 **Every one of the `8` permissive reasoning addresses this pass shelved is a text classifier or a text-generating conversational model.** None of them takes a biometric input. The register's permissive supply is, by construction, on the lawful side of the line — which is why `748-E`'s blocker never applied to it.

⚠️ **Two limits on this trend, stated rather than buried.** The Guidelines are **non-binding**, and the biometric qualifier is an *interpretation* of a text that omits it; and this pass could not reach a primary source to verify any of it (`T561`). Treat `T548` as the architecture to build toward and the question to put to the client's counsel in writing — not as settled law.

### 🔴 `T549` — do not pitch the medical-or-safety exception; wellbeing monitoring is exactly what it excludes

Article 5(1)(f) carries an exception for *medical or safety reasons*, and it is the first thing a client will reach for. 🔴 **It does not cover this register.** The reading returned this pass is explicit that the exception is narrow and that **monitoring wellbeing, motivation or learning satisfaction does not count as medical**. A deployer invoking it is additionally held to **necessity and proportionality**, and the inferences remain **personal data under the GDPR** even where the exception applies.

🔵 **Commercially this is good news, not bad.** The exception is the route a competitor will try to sell, and it is the route that fails an audit. The defensible architecture is the one that **never needs the exception** — `T548`'s text-only input line — and that is a design decision a studio can deliver and evidence.

### 🔴 `T550` — the timing is inverted against the way clients budget, and both halves moved in `2026`

| Instrument | Status in `2026` |
|---|---|
| **Article 5** prohibitions (incl. emotion inference in education) | 🔴 **In force since `2025-02-02`.** Already binding. Not a future obligation. |
| **Annex III** high-risk obligations for education AI | 🟢 **Postponed to `2027-12-02`** by the `2026` AI Omnibus (political agreement `2026-05-07`; amendments in force `2026-07-27`). Stand-alone systems `2027-12-02`; AI embedded in regulated products `2028-08-02`. |

🔴 **So in education AI the *ban* is live and the *compliance regime* is not.** A client who has budgeted an "EU AI Act readiness" programme for `2027` is budgeting for the wrong half: nothing they do in `2027` cures a prohibited architecture shipped in `2026`. 🔵 **Lead with Article 5, not Annex III** — it is the only part of the Act that can make this register's product illegal rather than merely expensive.

### 🔴 `T551` — the mandated trends leg reproduced `p758`'s superseded deadline, and `ACTION p758-A` caught it on its first opportunity

`p758` closed by adopting `ACTION p758-A`: *where this base already holds a dated instrument, its own record beats a fresh search result, and the conflict gets published.* 🔴 **One pass later the same leg returned the same bad date**: *"an April 2026 deadline for large public institutions to meet updated ADA accessibility guidelines for all web content, including vendor apps."*

🟢 **The rule worked exactly as written.** The base holds the **DOJ Interim Final Rule of `2026-04-20`** moving ADA Title II web-accessibility compliance to **`2027-04-26`** (public entities serving ≥`50,000`) and **`2028-04-26`** (smaller entities and special districts), WCAG 2.1 Level AA unchanged.

🔵 **The finding is the reproduction rate, not the date.** Two consecutive passes, same leg, same superseded figure, from different secondary sources. 🔴 **This is not a one-off defect in one article — it is the steady state of the trade press on this obligation**, and any pass that trusts the leg will publish it. `ACTION p758-A` is promoted from a rule to a **standing pre-write check** on every dated regulatory claim: `ACTION p759-B`.

### 🔴 `T552` — Primero's licence index is silent, and the byte-read is the only channel that resolves it

[`primeroIMS/primero`](https://github.com/primeroIMS/primero) is the UNICEF child-protection case-management platform and this base has carried the name for `127` mentions. 🔴 **GitHub names no licence for it.** The sidebar shows a link to a `LICENSE` file and the README says *"please carefully read our LICENSE"*, but the index displays **no licence type at all** — so every automated licence check this base or a client runs against it returns nothing.

🟢 **The byte-read is decisive.** `LICENSE` at `HEAD` is **`35,474 B`**, sha256₁₂ **`209c8853db16`**, and its structure is:

```
Primero™ is an application designed to help child protection workers … [5-line project preamble]
Copyright (c) 2014 UNICEF. All rights reserved.
This program is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify
it under the terms of the GNU Affero General Public License as
published by the Free Software Foundation, either version 3 …
------------------------------------------------------------------------
 GNU AFFERO GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE   Version 3, 19 November 2007   [full text]
```

🔴 **It is `AGPL-3.0`, and the index cannot see it because the file does not *begin* with the canonical text.** A project preamble and an `All rights reserved.` line ahead of the grant are enough to blind the detector. 🔵 **This is the inverse of every "index agrees" cell on these shelves**: the index is not wrong here, it is *absent*, and absence reads on a procurement checklist as "no licence found" — which is the most expensive possible wrong answer about an AGPL system.

### 🔴 `T553` — Primero is open code with a **gated configuration**, and the gate is in the licence file

🔴 **The repository does not contain the thing that makes Primero a child-protection system.** The same `LICENSE` preamble states that **the `CPIMS+` and `GBVIMS+` configurations (JSON bundles)** are obtained by writing to `childprotectioninnovation@gmail.com`. `CPIMS` and `GBVIMS` stand at **`3` mentions each** on these shelves — the base held the platform and not the gate.

🔵 **Name the pattern: open core by configuration.** The code is AGPL-3.0 and genuinely free; the domain model — forms, workflows, case taxonomies, the inter-agency data standards that make it CPIMS+ — is distributed under a request process with a human on the other end. 🔴 **An engagement that assumes `git clone` yields a deployable child-protection system is mis-scoped at the proposal stage.** Budget the configuration request as a dated dependency with no SLA, and start it before the statement of work is signed.

| [`techmatters/flex-plugins`](https://github.com/techmatters/flex-plugins) (**Aselo**) | 🔴 `AGPL-3.0` — `34,529 B`, `168adbc0ea70` | `12` |

🔵 **The generalisation is about who writes this software, not about licences.** Accessibility, sign-language and child-protection tools are built by **public universities, UN agencies and mission-driven non-profits**, and those authors choose AGPL deliberately — to stop a vendor closing a public good. 🟢 **So the pattern is predictable rather than unlucky**, and the correct response is architectural and is the same every time: the copyleft platform stays the **client's** self-hosted system of record, and Globant's work is a **separate process across an API** (`P292`). 🔴 What is never correct is embedding it in a hosted multi-tenant deliverable.

### 🔵 `T560` — two measurement findings about grants themselves, and one of them explains `T552`

🔵 **(a) Copyleft payloads are not byte-identifiable.** Measured this pass: **three distinct `AGPL-3.0` payloads** (`34,519` / `34,529` / `35,474 B`) and **two distinct `GPL-3.0` payloads** (`35,146 B` `c53a65c2fd56` and `35,148 B` `8b1ba204bb69`, differing only on `http://fsf.org` vs `https://fsf.org`). 🟢 By contrast `Apache-2.0` hit **`11,356 B` / `43070e2d4e53` on `5` of `5` canonical deliveries**. **So byte-equality identifies Apache-2.0 and cannot identify GPL/AGPL** — extends `649-R4`'s Apache work to the copyleft family, in the opposite direction.

🔴 **(b) `Apache-2.0` has a short-form delivery mechanism, and it blinds the index.** [`NVIDIA/NeMo-Guardrails`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/NeMo-Guardrails) ships `LICENSE.md` at **`653 B`**, sha256₁₂ `e08f3ab8c83a` — an `SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0` line plus the boilerplate notice, **not** the canonical `11,356 B` text. 🔴 **GitHub's sidebar names no licence for it either**, exactly as for Primero (`T552`). 🟢 **Second index-silent cell this pass, from a second mechanism** — a preamble ahead of the text, and a text replaced by an identifier. 🔵 **Both are invisible to the index and both are trivial for a byte-read**, which is the clearest justification this base has produced for the byte-read discipline itself.

| Channel | Result | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| `raw.githubusercontent.com` | 🟢 **`200`** on `25 / 25` probes | The byte-read discipline works for any public repository. |
| `github.com` HTML (via `curl`) | 🔴 **`378 B` JSON gate** | Not a `403` and not a `404`: a *session-scope* gate whose body names `add_repo`. |
| `api.github.com` | 🔴 **`403`** | No stars, no default branch, no archive flag. |
| fetch channel on `github.com/<owner>/<repo>` | 🟢 **reachable** | 🟢 The **only** source this pass had for ★, default branch, archive status and index-licence. |

🟢 **And the oracle discriminates in both directions, which this pass proved by accident.** `techmatters/aselo` — the Aselo address every secondary source implies — returned a licence miss *and* a README miss on the raw channel, which looks exactly like "a live repository with no grant." 🔴 **The fetch channel returned a true `404`: there is no such repository.** Three other misses this pass (`STATENet`, `DishmiDahara/student-mental-health-system`, `sont3r/student-early-warning`) returned `README.md` at `200` on the same raw channel and are therefore **live addresses with no grant** — a completely different finding, and the one that belongs on a refusal row.

🔵 **So the three states are now separable and all three were met in a single pass:** a **true `404`** (no repository), a **`378 B` session-scope gate** (repository exists, not attached to this session), and a **`200` README with no `LICENSE`** (repository exists, nothing granted). 🔴 **A pass that cannot tell the first from the third will publish a non-address as an ungranted one** — which this pass did for one address and caught in post-write verification.

🔴 **So the mandated `curl -sI` URL check is structurally unavailable for every repository outside this session's scope**, and a pass that ran it naively would read the gate's `378 B` body as a dead address and delete live rows. 🔵 **This refines `p749`'s "a `403` is not a `404`" into something sharper: a `200` is not a page.** Existence is confirmed on the fetch channel; `21 / 21` shelved addresses were confirmed there this pass. `ACTION p759-D`.

# 🆕 Trends new at `p758` (researched 2026-11-11) — `T533`–`T546`

**THE PASS'S MOST VALUABLE OUTPUT IS A DEFECT IN THE MANDATED RESEARCH, NOT A ROW.** The `AI {industry} industry trends {year}` leg returned a **dated compliance deadline that this base's own append-only log already refutes**. A pass that had trusted its own search results would have written a superseded federal deadline onto a sell shelf — and a client would have been sold urgency against a date the regulator moved seven months ago. The register is the **lecture-media captioning and accessible-media layer**.

### 🔴 `T533` — the trends leg returned a deadline this base had already corrected, and the correction was in its own logs

The leg surfaced, from a trade-press source, *"an April 2026 deadline for large public institutions to meet updated ADA accessibility guidelines, which is pushing institutions toward AI-enabled accessibility tools."*

🔴 **That deadline does not exist.** This base's own [`agents/trending.md`](../agents/trending.md) holds the DOJ **Interim Final Rule of `2026-04-20`**, which extended the ADA Title II web-accessibility compliance dates by one year: **`2027-04-26`** for public entities serving ≥`50,000` people and **`2028-04-26`** for smaller entities and special districts, with DOJ's own stated reason that it had *"overestimated the capabilities (whether staffing or technology) of covered entities to comply… in the time frames provided."* The technical standard — **WCAG 2.1 Level AA** — did not move.

🔵 **The generalisation, and it is the one to carry forward.** The supply legs have nilled for new rows ~`39` consecutive passes, which this base has treated as a cost. **This is worse than a nil: a nil is silent, and a stale date is confident.** Trade press re-publishes a regulatory date for years after a regulator changes it. 🟢 **Rule:** *no regulatory date enters a sell shelf from a search result alone when this base already holds a dated instrument on the same obligation — the base's own record wins, and the conflict is published.* `ACTION p758-A`.

`p749` wrote the document alt-format accessibility layer and registered the media layer explicitly as *"lecture-media captioning as its own register… the substrate is held and only the accessibility layer over it is missing."* Mention counts across the live shelves at the start of this pass:

### 🟢 `T535` — the agent nil is real, stable and four months old
