### 🔴 `T536` — the expensive gap is caption *measurement*, and the base held the recogniser without it for ~97 passes

[`openai/whisper`](https://github.com/openai/whisper) has sat on [`repos/foundations.md`](../repos/foundations.md) since `p661`, described as *"the permissive answer to captioning existing lecture video — the largest single remediation…"*. 🔴 **WCAG `1.2.2` does not require captions; it requires captions that are accurate.** Raw ASR output is not conformant, is widely litigated as non-conformant, and has a name in the disability community — *craptions*. A pipeline that ships whisper output as a deliverable ships a conformance claim it cannot support.

🟢 **Two permissive instruments close this and both were absent from every shelf:** [`jitsi/jiwer`](https://github.com/jitsi/jiwer) (`944★`, `Apache-2.0`, `11,338 B`, sha256₁₂ `e7fed65c1700`) for WER/MER/WIL, and [`revdotcom/fstalign`](https://github.com/revdotcom/fstalign) (`170★`, `Apache-2.0`, `11,345 B`, sha256₁₂ `fccc8c717e8f`) for FST alignment with NLP-aware normalisation and per-speaker breakdowns.

🔵 **Commercially this is the whole difference between a demo and a deliverable.** "We ran ASR over your estate" is unbillable past the pilot; "here is each file's measured accuracy against a human reference, with a regression baseline and a per-criterion review queue" is the engagement — and it is the offer that survives the deadline extension in `T533`, because the backlog is the same size either way.

### 🔴 `T537` — `audio description` was at `0` mentions across `757` passes, and it is a separate criterion with almost no supply

Audio description is **not** a caption variant. WCAG `1.2.3` (Level A, audio description *or* media alternative) and `1.2.5` (Level AA, audio description) are distinct criteria, and for a lecture that shows a diagram, a board derivation or a lab demonstration the caption track does not discharge them.

🔵 **Two registers, no shared authors, same stratification.** The hypothesis worth carrying: **the closer a component sits to the institutional record of a regulated decision, the more likely it is network-copyleft** — because those systems were built by public-sector and consortium funders who chose `AGPL` deliberately. 🔴 **Operationally: the licence conversation belongs in the first meeting of any record-system engagement, and the honest proposal is augmentation around the record rather than replacement of it.**

### 🔴 `T511` — instrument: ref `HEAD` beats `main`+`master`, and a `raw` `404` is not evidence of non-existence

🟢 **Change one, and it is free.** p755's script probed `main` **and** `master` × `5` filenames = up to `10` requests. Ref **`HEAD` resolves the repository's true default branch**, so one branch leg replaces two — **half the requests** — and `develop`/`dev`/`trunk` repositories stop scoring as false absences.
**Reproduction:** [`oat-sa/qti-sdk`](https://github.com/oat-sa/qti-sdk) → `main` **`404`**, `master` `200`, `develop` `200`, **`HEAD` `200`** (`18,025 B`). Any repository whose default is `develop` *only* was a false `NONE` in p755's instrument.

🔴 **Change two is a limit, not an improvement, and it changes how `84` rows must be reported.** `raw.githubusercontent.com` **does not follow repository renames or organisation moves.**
**Reproduction:** [`apereo/opencast`](https://github.com/apereo/opencast) → `404` on `README.md`, while **`opencast/opencast` → `200`**. Same project; the org moved.
🔴 So the verdict written to the ledger is **`unreadable-at-address`**, never `absent`. The channel that would separate *renamed* from *deleted* is `git ls-remote`, and it is **credential-denied in this session** (`p293`, `p755`). 🔵 **p755's single `NONE` label conflated three different facts** — no licence file, renamed, and deleted. This pass separates the first from the other two and declines to split the other two.

### 🔴 `T512` — a `200` on `LICENSE` is not a grant, and it failed three different ways in one sweep

**1. The R-package stub is a `POINTER`, not a grant** (`p307`'s three-valued classifier, now with a concrete population). Three repositories return `200` on `LICENSE` with a two-line metadata file:

| Repo | `LICENSE` bytes | Content | Real grant, from `DESCRIPTION` |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`rstudio/gradethis`](https://github.com/rstudio/gradethis) | `49 B` | `YEAR: 2021` / `COPYRIGHT HOLDER: Posit Software, PBC` | 🟢 **`MIT`** (`License: MIT + file LICENSE`) |
| [`sonsoleslp/tna`](https://github.com/sonsoleslp/tna) | `46 B` | `YEAR: 2025-2026` / `COPYRIGHT HOLDER: tna authors` | 🟢 **`MIT`** |
| [`ucbds-infra/ottr`](https://github.com/ucbds-infra/ottr) | `108 B` | adds `ORGANIZATION:` | 🟢 **`BSD-3-Clause`** |

🔵 **The R convention is `License: <SPDX> + file LICENSE`, where the file carries only the copyright *fields*.** A sweep that stops at the `200` records an unclassifiable grant; the grant is one fetch away in `DESCRIPTION`. **This sweep therefore refuses any payload under `40 B` as a pointer.**

**2. A `LICENSE` file can document the *absence* of a grant.** [`murderszn/open-tutor`](https://github.com/murderszn/open-tutor), `869 B`, `c341a936e405`: *"This repository has **not** declared a project-wide reuse license. This notice documents that status and **does not grant additional rights**."* 🔴 **Filed `no-grant`, from a `200`.**

**3. On a dual-licensed repository the canonical filename can hold the *other* grant.**

| Repo | `LICENSE` holds | the **code** grant is at |
|---|---|---|
| [`microsoft/autogen`](https://github.com/microsoft/autogen) | 🔴 **`CC-BY-4.0`**, `18,650 B` (docs) | 🟢 `LICENSE-CODE`, **`MIT`**, `1,141 B`, `c2cfccb812fe` |
| [`oaknational/oak-curriculum-ontology`](https://github.com/oaknational/oak-curriculum-ontology) | **`OGL-3.0`** for `ontology/`, `data/`, `docs/` | 🟢 `CODE-LICENSE`, **`MIT`**, for `scripts/`, `.github/` |

🔴 **A first-match glob on `LICENSE` reports `CC-BY-4.0` for the most-used multi-agent framework in this industry's stack.** 🟢 Oak's `OGL-3.0` half is the better news: UK Open Government Licence v3.0 **permits commercial exploitation with attribution**, so the curriculum ontology is usable — the row just needs two cells, not one.

### 🔴 `T514` — three corrections against this pass's own first readings

🔴 **1. A substring address match inflated the desynchronisation count `3.3×`.** The first reconciliation reported **`328`** shelf licence cells. Boundary-aware matching reports **`98`**. The defect: `a/b` matched **inside** `sebastianhab`**`a/b`**`ook-to-course-skill`, and `O/R` inside ordinary prose. **`233` of the `328` were licence tokens belonging to a *different* repository on the same line.** 🔵 **An address is only matched when neither neighbour is `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]`, and a licence is only attributed when it sits in its own table cell.**

🔴 **2. A `90`-character title block misread `4` BSD payloads as proprietary, because the BSD text's own words are "All rights reserved."** First reading filed [`jupyterhub/kerberosauthenticator`](https://github.com/jupyterhub/kerberosauthenticator), [`jupyterhub/yarnspawner`](https://github.com/jupyterhub/yarnspawner), [`mitodl/pylti`](https://github.com/mitodl/pylti) and [`uPortal-Project/CoursesPortlet`](https://github.com/uPortal-Project/CoursesPortlet) as *proprietary / all-rights-reserved*. **All four are BSD** (`BSD-3-Clause` ×3 at `1,492`/`1,492`/`1,529 B`; `BSD-2-Clause` for `pylti` at `1,316 B`). The distinguishing clause — *"Neither the name ... may be used to endorse"* — sits **past** the truncation. 🔵 `P171` says classify from the title block; **this is the counter-example that bounds it** — the title block is sufficient for *titled* texts and insufficient for notice-form GPL, untitled LGPL and every BSD variant. **`92` payloads were therefore re-read in full.**

🔴 **3. A keyword classifier read a *permission* as a *prohibition*.** `oaknational/oak-curriculum-ontology` was first filed `CC-BY-NC*` because the payload contains `non-commercially` — inside the sentence *"Exploit the information **commercially and non-commercially**"*, which is the **OGL-3.0 grant**. 🔵 **A NonCommercial verdict now requires either a titled `Attribution-NonCommercial` text or a matched prohibition clause**, never the bare token.

🟢 **All three were caught before publication and all three moved a verdict. `3` of this pass's own instruments were wrong on first use; the symmetric count against the shelves is `8` (`T513`).**

### 🔴 `T515` — the ledger's address harvester admits things that are not repositories, and `gate-address-shape` passes them

**`14` of the `84` unreadable rows are not addresses at all** (`evidence/unreadable-classes.2026-11-11-p756.tsv`). They are shape-valid `owner/repo`, so `gate-address-shape` (`p351`) accepts every one:

| Class | Rows | Specimens | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| **API-URL fragment** | 🔴 `6` | `repos/HKUDS`, `repos/moodle`, `repos/openedx`, `repos/gmilano`, `repos/dodona-edu`, `repos/packbackbooks` | harvested from `api.github.com/`**`repos/<owner>`**`/<repo>` — the *path prefix* was taken as the owner |
| documentation placeholder | `4` | `a/b`, `O/R`, `owner/repo`, `owner/name` | copied out of example snippets |
| **hyphen-truncated** | 🔴 `1` | `JushBJJ/Mr` | real repo is `JushBJJ/Mr-Ranedeer-AI-Tutor`, and 🔴 **that address is not in the ledger at all** — the truncation displaced it |
| `owner == repo` artefact | `3` | `gegok12/gegok12`, `hablala/hablala`, `iep-ui/iep-ui` | duplicated path segment |

🔵 **`a/b` had been carried since `p410` with `2` mentions across `2` passes, and `O/R` likewise.** They cost one `curl` each per sweep forever and they can never resolve.
🟢 **The fix is a shape rule, not a licence rule:** reject a leading segment of `repos`, reject a single-character segment, reject `owner == repo`, and flag any address that is a strict prefix of another ledger address at a hyphen boundary. **`ACTION p756-B`.**

### 🟢 `T519` — all four regional legs ran; three returned instruments and one returned a sixth consecutive nil

🟢 **LATAM is the best-measured region this pass, and the figures are adoption percentages — the thing this base has nilled for passes.** UNESCO **IESALC** (with UNU-IAS), across **`200` higher-education institutions in `19` countries**: **`87%`** use AI in at least one area and **`74%`** in teaching and learning, while only **`26%`** have a formal AI strategy, **`55%`** have **no AI budget**, and dedicated funding at **public** universities is **`4%`**. The **Digital Education Council** LATAM 2026 survey (with Tecnológico de Monterrey) reports **`92%` of students** and **`79%` of faculty** actively engaging with AI. UNESCO launched an **Observatory on AI in Education for Latin America and the Caribbean on `2026-04-14`**. Universidad de los Andes counts **`716` AI regulatory instruments across `23` countries**, `>80%` initiated since 2023.
🔵 **The usable read is the gap, not the adoption:** `87%` using against `26%` with a strategy and `4%` of public institutions funded. **Governance and funding are the billable layer; adoption already happened.**

Measured on `evidence/address-ledger.tsv` at `HEAD` before this pass touched it: **`3,749` newlines, of which `3,381` are `CRLF` and `368` are bare `LF`.** Every prior pass has counted this file with `wc -l` and `awk`, which split on `LF` and therefore see **`3,748` data rows** — the number `p745` reported and the number every count in `T505` uses. 🔴 **A parser that splits on `\r\n` instead — the technically correct reading of a CRLF file — sees only `3,381` records, because the `368` bare-`LF` lines are absorbed into the records above them.** The `315` `discovered-not-read` rows live in exactly that block: they are `315` rows under `awk` and effectively invisible under a CRLF split.

🔴 **This pass hit it directly.** The first ledger rewrite normalised every terminator to `LF` and produced a `3,399`-insertion / `3,381`-deletion diff — **a whole-file rewrite masquerading as a `40`-row update.** It was reverted and redone preserving `CRLF`, giving a `60` / `41` diff. 🟢 **Integrity verified after the redo: `0` addresses lost, `19` gained, and every verdict delta accounted for** (`unstated` `1,008` → `968` for the `40` swept; `no-grant` `149` → `175` for the `26` absences filed; `MIT` `1,187` → `1,201`).

🔵 **Three rules for `ACTION p755-A`, which will rewrite this file at scale:**
1. 🔴 **Preserve the existing terminator per record.** A normalising write destroys the diff and makes the change unreviewable.
2. 🔴 **State which parser produced any row count.** `3,748` (`LF`) and `3,381` (`CRLF`) are both correct readings of the same file, and quoting one without the other is how `315` rows go missing.
3. 🟢 **Verify by address-set difference, not by line count** — `comm -23` over the sorted address column is the check that actually caught this (`lost = 0`).
🔵 **Normalising the file to one terminator is the real fix, but it is a `3,381`-line diff and belongs in its own commit**, not inside a content pass.

# 🆕 Trends new at `p754` (researched 2026-11-10) — `T478`–`T489`

**Register: the early-childhood education and care (ECEC) layer, ages `0`–`8`.** `18` addresses probed, `15` licence payloads byte-read, `6` query denominators plus `20` shelf-mention counts measured, `3` index values materially corrected — **`3 / 3` toward a knowable grant**, `5` compliant grant-absences recorded as `T302` honest negatives. 🔴 **One legal claim corrected in the refusing direction against this base's own first reading (`T482`), and one instrument claim qualified (`T489`).**

### 🔴 `T478` — the register, and the shape of how it was missed

`753` passes of an *education* knowledge base held the sector that serves ages `0`–`8` at near-nil: `childcare` `0` mentions, `daycare` `0`, `nursery` `0`, `developmental screening` `0`, `ASQ` `0`, `ECERS` `0`, `parent engagement` `0`, `anganwadi` `0`, `foundational learning` `0`, `under-five` `0`, against `preschool` `3`, `pre-k` `3`, `kindergarten` `3`, `head start` `1`, `early childhood` `7`, `ECEC` `8`.

🟢 **The mechanism is worth recording because it will recur.** Every shelf on this base is headed *education*, and every row underneath silently assumed **a learner who is already enrolled in schooling** — with a timetable, a transcript, a faculty and an LMS. ECEC has none of those. Its buyer is a **municipality or a ministry of social development**, not a faculty; its practitioner is an **early-years educator or a community health worker**; its instrument is a **psychometric screen**, not an exam; and its delivery channel is a **parent**. 🔵 **`p752` learned that "employability" was several registers and `p753` that "accessibility" was four. `T478` is the same lesson applied to the base's own title word.**

### 🔴 `T481` — the market-sizing trap on this register: the *same year*, `42×` apart

"Daycare management software" is given as **`$11.09B` in `2026`** (→ `$13.93B` by `2030`, `5.9%` CAGR, Research and Markets) while "childcare management software" is given as **`$264.69M` in `2026`** (Mordor). 🔴 **That is a `~42×` divergence for adjacent category names in the same year, and it is a definition artefact, not growth or disagreement about growth.** The large figure plainly absorbs general-purpose centre operations — billing, payroll, compliance; the small one counts a specialist application category.

### 🔴 `T482` — CORRECTION, refusing direction: do not tell a client that Annex III names ECEC

🔴 **This pass's own first research leg returned the claim that EU AI Act Annex III names *"early childhood education and care (ECEC)"* explicitly. A second, targeted leg does not support that, and this base must not publish the first version.** What the measurements support:

- **Annex III point 3(a) text** covers AI systems used to determine **access or admission**, or to **assign** persons to, *"educational and vocational training institutions at all levels"*. 🔴 **The phrase "early childhood education and care" is not in the Annex text.**
- **The ECEC reading comes from the European Commission's *draft* guidelines**, which read *"at all levels"* broadly as covering early childhood, primary, secondary, tertiary, vocational and adult education, public or private, online or in person. 🔴 **Draft guidance is not the Regulation, and it is not final.**
- **Timing is disputed across sources.** Several place Annex III obligations at `2027-12-02`; the Digital Omnibus amendment's status was reported as unsettled (Council adoption / Official Journal publication) as of mid-`2026`. 🔴 **This base records the disagreement and asserts no date.**

⚠️ **Not primary-verified, and the reason is an instrument boundary:** `artificialintelligenceact.eu` and `eur-lex.europa.eu` **both fail DNS resolution under this session's network policy (`2 / 2`)**, exactly as `shibboleth.net` did at `p747`. See `ACTION p754-A`. 🟢 **The honest form of the finding is still commercially usable and is stronger for being accurate:** *an ECEC admission or placement system is very likely in scope of Annex III point 3(a) on the Commission's own reading of it, so design as if it is* — which is `T483`.

### 🟢 `T483` — the Article 6(3) split is an *architecture* boundary, not a compliance afterthought

The operative distinction in the same guidance: AI that provides **pedagogical support** may qualify for the **Article 6(3) filter** and fall outside high-risk, whereas **evaluative** uses that affect a learner's future remain high-risk regardless.

🟢 **For this register that draws a clean architectural line, and it is the single most actionable sentence this pass produced:**

- 🔴 **Evaluative, treat as high-risk** — eVaka's **placement and admission** decision; any developmental **screen** whose output routes a child to intervention; any school-readiness **determination**.
- 🟢 **Pedagogical/administrative, filter-candidate** — parent-facing content and guidance (Bebbo), educator planning and documentation support, the parent-report drafting workload, Kolibri content curation.

🔵 **Consequence for design: keep the agent out of the decision and on the evidence.** An agent that assembles, translates and explains the record for a human decision-maker, and never emits the placement or the screening verdict, is a different regulatory object from one that does. Every recipe at `P270`–`P274` is built on that separation.

### 🔴 `T484` — North America: the pre-K regulatory vacuum, measured

Per NASBE, as of **August `2026`**, **`37` US states have adopted AI guidance for public schools — few of them touch kindergarten, and pre-K is left out altogether.** Separately, **`16` states considered bills restricting classroom education technology in `2026` and `6` enacted them**; **Alabama's HB 78** pairs new **early-childhood screen-time standards** with required training for teachers and staff.

🔵 **Two consequences, and they point in opposite directions.** 🟢 A pre-K deployment faces **no state AI guidance to comply with** — unusually free ground. 🔴 But "no guidance" is not "no risk": it means the rules will be written *during* a multi-year engagement, and the enacted bills show the direction of travel is **restriction of screens for young children**. 🟢 **Design for it now: voice-first or screen-free interfaces, and educator-facing rather than child-facing AI, are the postures that survive the rule that has not been written yet** — which is why [`nikjain15/toddler-learning-companion`](https://github.com/nikjain15/toddler-learning-companion) (MIT, voice-first, screen-free) is on the agents shelf despite `0★`.

### 🔴 `T485` — the register's defining licence structure: the code is open, the instrument is not

In ECEC the asset with value is a **validated psychometric instrument** — a question set with published norms — and the dominant ones are **commercial copyrighted products**: **ASQ-3** (Brookes), **Denver II** (Denver Developmental Materials, Inc.), **M-CHAT-R/F**. 🔴 **An MIT or Apache-2.0 grant on a screening application conveys no right whatsoever to the instrument inside it.**

🟢 **The compliant pattern is already visible in the two honest projects on the shelf**, which is why they earned rows at `3★` and `0★`:

- [`hsongra11/mychild-app`](https://github.com/hsongra11/mychild-app) (Apache-2.0) **substitutes** a public-domain bank — CDC-derived milestones — and states that it avoids ASQ-3, M-CHAT-R/F and Denver.
- [`khorihutama/tumbuh-kembang`](https://github.com/khorihutama/tumbuh-kembang) **carves its Denver II–derived dataset out of its own MIT grant** and disclaims affiliation.

🔴 **In an engagement this is a funded work package — instrument licensing, or the client's own validated content — never a scrape.** 🟢 Public-domain substrates that *are* usable: **CDC milestone checklists** and, for population measurement, instruments published for open use by multilateral bodies. `P271` is built entirely around this constraint.

### 🟢 `T486` — APAC is the only region where the **state** ships ECE AI at scale

- **China.** The Ministry of Education with four other departments launched an **"AI + Education" action plan in April `2026` that explicitly spans early childhood through lifelong learning** — the only national AI-in-education plan found this pass that names the early years. Scale: **~`36M` children across `250,000`+ kindergartens**. Research is already operational rather than aspirational: a `2026` study tests **LLMs as assessment teammates for teacher–child interaction quality** in Chinese preschools, framing AI as the only way quality monitoring at that scale becomes feasible. A March `2026` study of `50` Froebelian practitioners found a **"dual-track"** practice — hands-on nature-based play alongside AI personalisation — with explicit concern about displacing sensory experience.
- **India.** Public pre-primary runs through **~`1.37M` anganwadi centres** under ICDS, with nutrition tracked via **Poshan Tracker**; the **first "AI-powered anganwadi"** (Waddhamna, near Nagpur) uses VR, smartboards and tablets with plans to scale to `40` more. 🔴 **But the curriculum policy excludes the early years: AI and computational thinking enter from Class `3` in the `2026`–`27` session**, while the `3`–`6` band — where AI literacy arguably starts — is not addressed.

🟢 **Commercially this is the register's clearest opportunity, and `T488` explains why nobody has taken it:** the demand is state-scale and named, and the permissive substrate that fits it ([`dimagi/commcare-hq`](https://github.com/dimagi/commcare-hq), `BSD-3-Clause`) is already the family deployed under the anganwadi network. `P272`.

### 🟢 `T487` — the register's only real agent is Australian, MIT, and *safety-aware* by design

[`MengC-OvO/easy-teaching`](https://github.com/MengC-OvO/easy-teaching) — **`58★`, MIT** (`1,082 B`, sha256₁₂ `f755cdc76e68`), Python, pushed `2026-09-16` — is a **safety-aware teacher agent for Australian early-childhood education**, and it is simultaneously the highest-starred permissive artefact in the register and one of only two repositories the `early childhood education stars:>20` query returns at all.

🔵 **"Safety-aware" is the finding, not the adjective.** In ECEC the binding constraint on an agent is **duty of care** — what it must not say to or about a child, what it must escalate to a human, what it must refuse. 🟢 **An agent for this sector that treats those constraints as the product rather than as a guardrail bolted on afterwards is the correct shape**, and this is the one public implementation of it. 🔴 At `58★` and single-author it is a pattern to learn from and extend, not a dependency to deploy.

🟢 **The policy layer in LATAM is real and ahead of its supply.** **Chile**: the Ministry of Science presented a new **AI policy with `100`+ actions committed for `2026`**; Mineduc's curricular-bases work addresses AI **from the preschool stage**, and it published *"PotencIA el aprendizaje"* (`2025`) as explicitly non-prescriptive guidance; the **6th Congress on Innovation in Early Childhood Education (CIEI `2026`)** carries a responsible-AI-in-*educación inicial* track. **Mexico**: the Presidency and SEP opened a national debate on AI, social media and devices in schools, with forums toward a law covering minors' use of platforms and AI; SEP ran a generative-AI survey drawing **`1.5M`+ student responses**; **MXN `284.1M`** was allocated to teacher professional development in `2026`, a figure specialists call insufficient. 🔵 **Reading: LATAM is a *demand-led* ECEC opportunity, not a supply-led one.** The region has the policy mandate, the public-provision scale and (via Chile) explicit preschool AI curriculum intent, with no domestic open stack to build on — so the engagement shape is to bring `commcare-hq` or `kolibri` and localise, not to adopt a regional platform.

# 🆕 Trends new at `p753` (researched 2026-11-10) — `T465`–`T477`

**Register: the Deaf-learner and sign-language access layer.** `35` addresses probed, `24` licence payloads byte-read, `16` query denominators plus `2` licence-distribution samples measured, `3` index values materially corrected — **all three in the refusing direction**, which is unusual for this base and is the register's signature. 🔴 **One cross-shelf stale date corrected: six shelves assert an "April 2026 ADA deadline" as a live demand driver and the deadline moved in April 2026 (`T475`).**

### 🔴 `T465` — the register, and the shape of how it was missed

`p749` took the **print-disability** estate — DAISY, `liblouis`, `readium`, `epubcheck` — and did it well. **Print disability and deafness are different estates with different publishers, different technology and different law**, and the second was at near-nil across `752` passes: `vlibras` `0` mentions, `signwriting` `0`, `sign language processing` `0`, `montreal forced` `0`, `common voice` `0`, `WLASL` `1`, `sign.mt` `1`, `Deaf` `7`. 🟢 **The lesson is the one `p752` reached from the other direction: "accessibility" is not a register — it is four registers, and holding one of them well is not coverage of the others.**

### 🔴 `T466` — the direction asymmetry, and it is the commercial fact of the register

`sign language recognition` → **`10,467`** repositories; `sign language translation` → **`4,980`**; `sign language avatar synthesis` → **`6`**; `sign language production avatar` → **`4`**. Education consumes the **text → sign** direction, because a Deaf learner is a receiver of institutional content; the open-source field supplies the **sign → text** direction, because that is what a hearing institution wants in order to read a Deaf person's input. **Ratio ≈ `2,600 : 1` against the direction education needs.** 🟢 **A studio that can assemble a production pipeline is not competing with ten thousand repositories — it is competing with four.**

### 🔴 `T467` — `sign` is a colliding token, third reproduction in three passes

`sign language mcp server` → `12`, of which **`0`** are sign-language artefacts (an e-signature MCP at `142★`, motor-current **signature** analysis, **signed** drone approvals). `sign language agent llm` → `14`, of which **`0`** are. 🔵 **`p751`'s `T444` (timetabling), `p752`'s `T456` (ESCO/escolar), now `T467` (sign/signature).** The generalisation is now firm enough to state as instrument policy: **a `total_count` on a query whose head word is a common English or Romance stem is an upper bound, not a measurement, and must be read result-by-result before it is published.** 🟢 **The corrected reading — there is no sign-language agent or MCP layer in open source at all — is a stronger finding than the inflated one.**

### 🔴 `T468` — the ownership event: this field's reference stack is now a US for-profit's, and only the bytes show it

### 🔴 `T475` — the cross-shelf stale date: the April 2026 ADA Title II deadline moved, in April 2026

**Six shelves of this base** — `agents/trending.md`, `repos/foundations.md` (four occurrences), `repos/trending.md`, `verticals/solutions.md` and `intel/market.md` — assert an **"April 2026 ADA deadline for large US public institutions"** as a **live demand driver**, in some places as the named reason a captioning row matters. **It moved:**

| What | Date |
|---|---|
| DOJ **Interim Final Rule** published (`91 FR 20902`) | **`2026-04-20`** |
| Old compliance date for public entities ≥ `50,000` population | `2026-04-22` *(the date this base's shelves encode as "April 2026")* |
| 🔴 **New compliance date, entities ≥ `50,000`** | 🔴 **`2027-04-26`** |
| 🔴 **New compliance date, entities < `50,000`** | 🔴 **`2028-04-26`** |
| Technical standard — **unchanged** | **WCAG 2.1 Level AA** |
| Public comment window on the IFR | to `2026-06-22`; DOJ signalled a possible later NPRM on substantive changes |
| Separate HHS Section 504 IFR (funding recipients) | `2026-05-11` → **`2027-05-11`** |

🔴 **What did *not* change, and it is the half a vendor deck omits:** DOJ stated in the IFR that covered entities **retain their ongoing Title II obligation** to make digital services accessible. The deadline for the *rule's* technical conformance moved; the underlying duty did not, and litigation risk under the general obligation is unaffected.

🟢 **The commercial reading, and it is better news than it sounds:** the sales motion changes from **deadline panic** to **two budget cycles**. An institution that was being sold a remediation sprint can now be sold a programme — captioning, then signed tracks, then procurement standards — and the signed-track work in this register, which could not have been scoped inside a six-month panic, fits inside `2027-04-26`.

### 🔴 `T476` — the EMEA driver for this register is *not* the European Accessibility Act, and the gap is the finding

**EN 301 549 V4.1.1 was published `2026-09-02`** by ETSI/CEN/CENELEC and maps directly onto the EAA's essential accessibility requirements. 🔴 **But the EAA does not mandate sign language in education.** Its sign-language expectations attach to **audiovisual media services** (interpretation for TV and streaming) and to **video-capable interactive computing devices** — not to educational provision. The European Union of the Deaf puts **~1 million deaf sign-language users in the EU/EEA** and has an EAA-implementation shortcomings report in progress. 🟢 **So in EMEA the legal driver for a signed track in education is national disability law plus **UNCRPD Article 24**, not the EAA — and a proposal that cites the EAA at a ministry will be corrected in the room.** 🔵 This is recorded as an **informed gap**: the instrument exists, it is current, and it does not reach this register.

# 🆕 Trends new at `p751` (researched 2026-11-10) — `T439`–`T452`

**Added above `p750`'s `T426`–`T438`.** `p751` changed the register to **scheduling, matching and resource allocation** — the constraint solver under the timetable, the exam diet, the room, the bus and the school place. `41` addresses probed, `33` licence-payload probes, **`31` payloads byte-read**, **`5` index values materially corrected (`5 / 5` toward a knowable grant)**, `21` query denominators measured, `5` boundary rows recorded not shelved, all `5` regional blocks written. 🔴 **Two of the fourteen findings are defects in *this base's own* licence instrument, both reproducible, and they invalidate byte constants written before this pass.**

Reading a licence through shell command substitution strips the trailing newline. **Five** distinct Apache-2.0 payload hashes were read in a `52`-byte band, and **two collide on byte count**: `c71d239df917` (`11,357 B`, stock), `58d1e17ffe51` (**`11,357 B`**, stock + leading blank line − trailing newline, `UniTime/unitime`), `cfc7749b96f6` (`11,358 B`, stock + leading blank line — `or-tools`, `timefold-solver`, `scip`), `94d81cb282da` (`11,344 B`, `cvxpy`), `df825c8e037a` (`11,396 B`, `ORLM`). 🔴 **Quote the hash, never the size.**

`Project-OSRM/osrm-backend` returned no grant at `8` probed paths and would have been published as a false `T302` negative. `raw.githubusercontent.com` is case-sensitive: `LICENSE.txt` → `404`, **`LICENSE.TXT` → `200`**, BSD-2-Clause, `1,297 B`, `df207517bc08`. 🟢 **Corrected chain, to be used by every successor pass:** `LICENSE, LICENSE.md, LICENSE.txt, LICENSE.TXT, COPYING, COPYING.txt, COPYING.md, LICENSE-APACHE, LICENSE.rst, LICENCE, license`. Second instance of the `724-I` case-sensitivity class.

`scheduling mcp server` **`991`** and `optimization mcp server` **`893`** against `school timetabling mcp server` **`9`**, `timetabling agent llm` **`7`**, `natural language to constraint programming` **`4`**, `school assignment deferred acceptance` **`3`**, `exam scheduling llm agent` **`2`**, `constraint model llm education` **`1`**. Roughly **`110 : 1`** against the vertical. This is `p747`'s `T402` shape repeating in a new tier: the horizontal capability exists, the education specialisation does not.

### 🔴 `T444` — `school timetabling mcp server` matches a different word, and what it matches is organically EMEA

**`8 / 9` results *read* a timetable out of a national school portal; `1` *builds* one.** The portals are European — EduPage (🇸🇰), Pronote (🇫🇷), WebUntis (🇦🇹🇩🇪), Bakaláři (🇨🇿) — plus Comci (🇰🇷). 🔵 **Nobody placed this supply by region; the supply placed itself where the portal has a national install base.** `p738`'s `738-B` class ("the keyword legs are matching a different word"), now with a regional consequence.

### 🔴 `T445` — FET is in the `T359` dead state *and* its upstream is unreachable

`lalescu/fet` → `404`, `fet-timetabling/fet` → `404`; **`lalescu.ro` and `lalescu.ro/liviu/fet/` both `000` (`2 / 2`)**. The highest-starred GitHub artefacts are third-party copies last pushed **2019** (`sisardor/FET-scheduling-system`, `14★`, **no licence**) and **2018** (`karandit/fet`, `5★`, index `AGPL-3.0`, `LICENSE` → `404`). Second instance of `p747`'s `T396` Shibboleth pattern: **a widely-deployed tool that a GitHub-only instrument cannot see.**

### 🔴 `T446` — Chile's SAE: nationally deployed, fully published, and not open source

An adaptation of Gale–Shapley deferred acceptance allocates school places nationally; the algorithm, rules, data and a simulator are published; under the law-adapted stability notions **a stable assignment may not always exist**, so ties are broken **at the family level**. 🔴 **The implementation is not public:** `ConsiliumBots`, which held the `2022–2024` Ministry maintenance contract, has `7` public repositories and the mechanism is not among them — only `school-choice-dashboard` (**MIT**, `0★`, `2025-05-20`). 🟢 **Pattern public, code private — favourable, because the defensible part is the published mechanism.**

### 🟡 `T447` — OptaPlanner is archived; Timefold is the successor, by the same team

`apache/incubator-kie-optaplanner`: `3,513★`, `archived=true`, last push `2026-07-14`, `README.md` → `404`. **Timefold was forked from OptaPlanner on `2023-04-20` by the original OptaPlanner team**, stated in `timefold-solver`'s own `README`. The archive notice names `apache/incubator-kie-drools`, whose raw channel answers `200` but which the `repo:` search channel does not return. 🔵 **Never put OptaPlanner in a proposal; it is the name a studio reaches for first.**

### 🔴 `T448` — two pollution modes in this register's discovery channel, both measured

(i) `or-tools mcp server` sorted by stars returns `Dataojitori/nocturne_memory` at **`1,426★`** — a memory server with no optimisation content — above every real row, whose true top is `22★`: **an unread star-sorted head is `60×` wrong here.** (ii) `student sectioning` returns **`2,970`** repositories by matching two common words independently; the real artefact is one repository inside UniTime.

### 🔴 `T449` — the AI Act boundary that depends on the implementation, not the function

Allocating a school place is **Annex III point 3(a)**. But the Act regulates *AI systems*, and a hand-written CP-SAT or MIP model is rules defined entirely by natural persons — the category the definition is generally read to exclude. 🔴 **The same business function may therefore sit inside or outside Annex III depending on how it is built:** an explicit constraint model or a deferred-acceptance mechanism plausibly out, an LLM that *infers* constraints or a learned applicant ranker plausibly in. 🟢 **A real architectural lever — keep the LLM on the authoring side and let a human approve each constraint before it binds.** ⚠️ **An open legal reading requiring counsel, not settled law**, and it cuts both ways: prototyping with an LLM can convert an unregulated scheduler into a high-risk system. ⚠️ **The date is disputed:** most sources say Annex III point 3 applies from **`2027-12-02`** after the Digital Omnibus on AI, **Regulation (EU) 2026/1744** (OJ `2026-07-24`); at least one argues point 3 was not amended. **This base does not pick a side.**

### 🔴 `T450` — the licence seam in this register runs between the general and the vertical

🟢 **General-purpose solvers: `13 / 13` permissive** (Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD-3, BSD-2, MPL-2.0), no copyleft at all. 🔴 **Education-specific solving: copyleft wherever it exists** — `UniTime/cpsolver` **LGPL-3.0** sitting under Apache-2.0 `UniTime`, `yuroyami/FET-MCP` **AGPL-3.0**, `karandit/fet` indexed **AGPL-3.0**, FET itself GPL-family. 🟢 **Reading: the permissive education scheduler is an unoccupied position — build on `or-tools` or `timefold-solver`, do not extend `cpsolver` or FET.** The inverse of `p750`'s seam, where measuring was permissive and record-holding was copyleft.

### 🟢 `T451` — `5` index corrections, `5 / 5` toward a knowable grant, `0` in the refusing direction

`MiniZinc/libminizinc` → **MPL-2.0** (with a per-file header carve-out); `Pyomo/pyomo` → **BSD-3-Clause** (Sandia, `DE-NA0003525`, US Government retains certain rights); `coin-or/pulp` → **MIT**; `jump-dev/JuMP.jl` → **MPL-2.0** (grant stated in prose above the text, which is why the index missed it); `valhalla/valhalla` → **MIT** (via `T442`). 🔵 **In this register `NOASSERTION` means "the index could not parse a composite or pointer grant", not "there is no grant"** — the opposite of its meaning in `p746`'s `winterop-com` rows, where the payload was actively proprietary.

### 🔴 `T452` — the register's agent head is stale, and the freshest row is the smallest

The highest-starred agent in the register, `Jacck/mcp-ortools` (`22★`), was last pushed **`2024-12-26`** — `23` months. The freshest, `PraveshKoirala/optimization-mcp` (pushed `2026-07-27`), has **`1★`**. `teshnizi/OptiMUS` (`308★`) is `12` months stale and `Cardinal-Operations/ORLM` (`283★`) `14` months; the `2026` follow-up literature (ORPilot, Opti-Agent-Bench, VeriSimpl) produced **papers this pass found no maintained permissive code for**. 🔵 **Treat every agent row in this register as a reference implementation, not a dependency** — the maintained artefacts here are the *solvers*, not the agents.


# 🆕 Trends new at `p750` (researched 2026-11-10) — `T426`–`T438`

**Added above `p749`'s `T417`–`T425`.** `p750` changed the register to **student wellbeing and
safeguarding** — the duty of care: screening, monitoring, disclosure, case management and the
early-warning function that sits under retention. `45` addresses probed, `30` licence-payload probes,
**`26` payloads byte-read**, **`11` index values materially corrected**, `4` `T302` grant-absences with
no denominator claimed, `5` addresses in the `T359` dead state, **`37` query denominators measured**.

🔴 **The one-line reading of the pass: in this register the institution is required to monitor, forbidden
to infer affect, and has nothing to buy in the open — and the one capability with abundant open-source
supply (`8,216` repositories) is the exact capability EMEA prohibits.**

> ⚠️ **Numbering note.** The strings `T427`, `T429` and `T430` also occur in this base's pre-reset
> trending history as unrelated dangling cross-references, flagged at `p733` and never renumbered. The
> definitions below are authoritative on the live shelves.

## T426 — 🔵 The four-channel instrument state is re-controlled and `T417`/`T418` hold a second time

`2` controls per channel, one proven-alive address and one invented address, run this pass:

| Channel | Alive address | Invented address | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `curl -sI https://github.com/{owner}/{repo}` | **`403`** | **`403`** | 🔴 **No discriminating power.** ⚠️ And the *first* line of output is the proxy's `HTTP/1.1 200 Connection Established` — read the status code, not the first line. |
| `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}` | **`403`** + explicit session-scope message | — | 🔴 Scope-refused for every repository outside this session's grant. |
| `gh api -X GET search/repositories -f q=repo:{owner}/{name}` | `total_count` **`1`** with full metadata | **`422` Validation Failed** | 🟢 **The working metadata channel.** `422` or `total_count == 0` is the genuine `T359` dead-address signal. |
| `raw.githubusercontent.com/{owner}/{repo}/{branch}/{path}` | **`200`** | **`404`** | 🟢 **The working bytes channel.** |

🔵 **Nothing new, and that is the point:** this is the third consecutive pass to reproduce the same four
states, so the channel map can now be treated as stable rather than re-derived each pass.

## T427 — 🟢 The layer seam, fifth confirmation, and now stated as a law: *measuring is permissive, holding the record is copyleft*

| Layer | Rows | Licences observed | Crossovers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sensing, instrumentation, measurement | `7` | BSD-3-Clause ×`5`, Apache-2.0 ×`2` | **`0`** |
| The record about the person | `4` | AGPL-3.0 ×`3`, CPAL-1.0 ×`1` | **`0`** |

Five independent estates now agree (`T360` the platform/agent seam, `T410` the eligibility-engine seam,
`T423` the checker/assistive-runtime seam, and this). 🟢 **Portable consequence:** in any education
engagement, assume the system of record is copyleft and the measurement library is not, and design the
process boundary *before* the architecture review rather than after it (`P253`).

## T428 — 🔴 The safeguarding classifier tier has exactly one maintained, permissive, broad-coverage member

[`meta-llama/PurpleLlama`](https://github.com/meta-llama/PurpleLlama) (`4,473★`) is the strongest
artefact and is **not open source**: the `7,669 B` payload is the `LLAMA 3.2 COMMUNITY LICENSE
AGREEMENT`, with the Acceptable Use Policy incorporated by reference, a `700 million MAU` commercial

`1,005★`) last shipped `2024-11-22`. 🟢 **The answer is
[`ibm-granite/granite-guardian`](https://github.com/ibm-granite/granite-guardian)** — Apache-2.0,
pushed `2026-10-16`, and at `189★` it is `4.2%` of Llama Guard's visibility. 🔵 **Record this as a
procurement finding, not a technical one:** a studio that reaches for the obvious artefact here imports
a use restriction into a client's safeguarding system.

## T429 — 🔴 The entire open-source early-warning tier is `7 / 7` at `0★` and `6 / 7` without a usable grant

Enumerated in full on [`../agents/top.md`](../agents/top.md). All seven are built on the same two public
datasets (OULAD and the UCI dropout set); the single licensed member is MIT with `0★`. 🟢 **The honest
client statement: there is no system to adopt, there is a recipe to implement** — and the components
that make it defensible (`OpenLRW` for the record store, `OnTask` for the intervention, a subgroup
audit for the fairness claim) are all held and all permissive-or-ECL. See `P254`.

## T430 — 🔴 The capability with `8,216` repositories behind it is the one capability EMEA forbids

`facial emotion recognition` returns **`8,216`** repositories; `emotion recognition education` returns
`44`; `attention detection classroom` returns `55`. Meanwhile the agent layer this register actually
needs is a measured desert: `student retention agent llm` **`0`**, `child protection mcp` **`0`**,
`early warning agent education` `2`, `school safety llm agent` `2`, `mental health mcp server` `8`.

🔴 **And the abundant capability is a per-se prohibition in the EU.** AI Act **Article 5(1)(f)** bans
AI systems that infer emotions of natural persons **in the workplace and in education institutions**,
applicable since **`2025-02-02`** with **no grace period**, subject only to a narrow *medical or safety*
exception. Inferring student attention or interest, detecting affect during an admission test, and
adding affect detection to proctoring are the worked examples the commentary converges on.

🟢 **The operational rule, and it is the most useful sentence in this pass:** *every open-source
component a wellbeing build needs is a classifier of **content** (text, image, URL), not of
**affect** — and that is a legal requirement in EMEA, not a design preference.* `P251` is written to
that constraint.

wellbeing app cannot be built on it without negotiating the attribution clause.** This extends `T419`'s
two causes (title block is a project name; composite of vendored grants) with a third: **an uncommon but
real licence family**.

## T435 — 🔴 Read the first *paragraph* of the payload, not the title block: three composite shapes in one pass

| Repository | Shape |
|---|---|
| `GantMan/nsfw_model` | Title block is a **disclaimer** — *"contains third-party copyrighted material under different licenses"* — and the grant (`MIT`) appears on line `4`. |

🟢 **Rule for this base's classifier, stated as a gate:** a verdict may be taken from the title block
**only** when the first `4` lines contain no disclaimer, no per-directory enumeration and no second
licence name. Otherwise the whole payload must be scanned. `p750` found `3 / 26` payloads failing that
test — an `11.5%` rate, which is too high to classify from the head alone.

## T436 — 🔴 The EMEA pincer: the same institution is *required to monitor* and *forbidden to infer affect*

- **Required.** The UK's **Keeping Children Safe in Education 2026** was published `2026-07-07` and is in
  force from **`2026-09-01`**. It makes the filtering-and-monitoring review an at-least-annual,
  evidenced duty (reported at **paragraph 171**), and the DfE standards now ask whether systems can
  handle *"real-time, dynamic, personalised and AI-generated content"*, pointing schools at the DfE's
  **Generative AI: Product Safety Expectations (January 2026)**. Commentary reports that filtering must
  block tools capable of generating or altering sexually explicit imagery.
- **Forbidden.** AI Act **Article 5(1)(f)** — affect inference in education, prohibited since
  `2025-02-02`.

🟢 **Design consequence, and it is sellable:** the compliant architecture monitors **content and
behaviour signals** and never **emotional state**; the evidence pack for the annual review is a
deliverable in its own right. ⚠️ **Date caution carried from `p748`:** the `Regulation (EU) 2026/1744`
citation and the `2027-12-02` high-risk date remain single-source in this base and are reported, not
asserted.

## T437 — 🔴 The North America gate is **consent**, it is dated, and it is being enforced right now

- The US Department of Education's **August 2026** student-privacy guidance states that for behavioural
  health screeners probing emotional or psychological states, schools must obtain **written parental
  consent before administration** — grounded in **PPRA**, which covers surveys touching on *"mental or
  psychological problems of the student or the student's family"*.
- 🔴 **Live enforcement:** the Department's Student Privacy Policy Office has **demanded Illinois revise**
  its guidance on conducting mental-health screenings without parental consent and on holding results
  outside the education record, with an **ISBE response deadline of `2026-11-13`** — three days after
  this pass. Its stated position is that *"temporary records"*, separate repositories and withholding
  from parents all infringe FERPA parental rights.
- The amended **COPPA** rule carries a compliance deadline of **`2026-04-22`**, with separate parental
  consent required for AI training uses; a school's consent covers educational use only.

🟢 **Consequence for a proposal:** in North America the consent flow and the records architecture are
**the first two work packages**, not compliance appendices, and a screening product that stores results
outside the education record is now an identified legal risk rather than a privacy nicety (`P252`).

## T438 — 🔴 The market-sizing nil: the two segments this register sells into are not sized anywhere

The mandated market leg and a targeted sweep returned **no published sizing for school-safety
monitoring or for student-success / retention platforms**. The nearest adjacent series disagree by a
factor of **`2.7×`** on the same year: digital mental health `2026` estimates span **`$11.69B` to
`$32.06B`**; mental-health technology is put at **`$6.43B` (2026) → `$15.8B` (2035) @ `10.5%`** by one
house and **`$7.48B` (2025) → `$8.6B` (2026) @ `15.5%`** by another; a campus-specific series reads
**`$4.95B` (2025) → `$17.27B` (2034)** with **North America at `42%`** of `2025`. 🟢 **Published as a
conflict, not averaged** — and the segment nil is the more useful fact: *quote the obligation, not the
market.* The obligation has dates (`T436`, `T437`); the market does not have a number.

# 🆕 Trends new at `p749` (researched 2026-11-10) — `T417`–`T425`

**Added above `p748`'s `T409`–`T416`.** `p749` changed the register to **alternative-format
production** — what converts a course document into something a blind, low-vision or dyslexic student
can actually use. `39` addresses probed, **`20` licence payloads byte-read**, `18 / 20` agreeing with
the index, **`2` `T302` grant-absences recorded with no denominator claimed**, **`2` canonical
literature addresses found dead**, `1` MPL-2.0 boundary row recorded rather than shelved.

🔴 **The one-line reading of the pass: the deadline moved, the obligation did not, and the two things
institutions are actually bought for return `0` repositories each.**

## T417 — 🔴 The URL-verification channel this register is specified to use is closed here, and a `403` is not a `404`

`curl -sI https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>` returns **`403`** on `3 / 3` hosts probed. The agent
proxy does not pass `github.com` HTML at all. ⚠️ **This is the most dangerous instrument state the base
has hit**, because the failure is silent and uniform: a pass that treated `403` as "address does not
exist" would delete correct shelves wholesale and report the deletion as diligence.

**The corrected channel, in two parts, both confirmed working this pass:**

- **Existence, licence, stars, default branch, archived flag** → `gh api -X GET search/repositories -f q="repo:<owner>/<name>"`. `total_count == 0` **or** HTTP **`422`** is the genuine "not a canonical current address" signal (the `T359` state).
- **Licence payload bytes** → `raw.githubusercontent.com/<owner>/<name>/<default_branch>/<path>`. `20 / 20` reads succeeded on paths that exist.

## T418 — 🔴 `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>` is scope-refused while `gh api search/repositories` answers for the same repository

`repos/*` returns **`403`** with an explicit session-scope message for every repository outside this
session's grant. `search/repositories` answers for those identical repositories, with `license.spdx_id`,
`stargazers_count`, `default_branch`, `pushed_at` and `archived` all present. 🔵 **So "GitHub API blocked"
is too coarse a claim for this base to keep making** — it is the *per-repo* endpoint that is blocked
and the *search* endpoint that is not. Earlier passes recorded the API as unavailable; that was half right.

## T419 — 🔴 `NOASSERTION` has two distinct causes in this tier, and conflating them mis-advises a client

| Row | Index | Payload | Cause |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blindpandas/bookworm` | `NOASSERTION` | `18,693 B`, line `3` reads **`SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later`** | Title block is the **project name**, so the classifier cannot match. 🟢 **The licence is knowable with certainty.** |
| `ryersondmp/sa11y` | `NOASSERTION` | `21,244 B` naming **MIT ×`25`**, **ISC ×`3`** | A **composite** of vendored dependency licences over an MIT project. 🟡 Knowable, but it needs a legal reading rather than a `grep`. |

🔴 **The first is a classifier defect and should be overridden on the payload. The second is a genuine
licence-composition question and should be escalated.** A shelf that writes "NOASSERTION — avoid" for both
loses a `192★` platform for no reason, and waves through a composite that a client's counsel will stop.

## T420 — 🔴 The grant of the most consequential program in this tier sits at a lowercase path and has no SPDX identifier

`nvaccess/nvda` publishes at **`copying.txt`**, `53,408 B`. All `6` capitalised paths this base probes
return `404`, and so does `COPYING.txt` — **the case is load-bearing**. The payload is self-describing and
authoritative over per-file headers:

> *NVDA is available under the GNU General Public License version 2 or later, **with two special exceptions**.*

The exceptions are **"Non-GPL Components in Plugins and Drivers"** and **"Microsoft Distributable Code"**.
🔵 **The honest statement is "GPL-2.0-or-later with two exceptions", not "unlicensed".** This matters
because NVDA is not a dependency — it is the **test target**: it is free, so it is what students use, so it
is what an institution's content has to work in. Every accessibility engagement touches it.

## T421 — 🔴 `default_branch` is load-bearing, and in this estate it is the majority case

`6` of `18` rows publish from neither `main` nor `master`:

| Repository | Default branch |
|---|---|
| `IBMa/equal-access` | `main-4.x` |
| `dequelabs/axe-core` | `develop` |
| `Speech-Rule-Engine/speech-rule-engine` | `develop` |
| `edrlab/thorium-reader` | `develop` |
| `blindpandas/bookworm` | `develop` |
| `veraPDF/veraPDF-library` | `integration` |

🔴 **A licence probe hard-coded to `master` would have returned `404` on all six and this pass would have
published six fabricated grant-absences.** Confirms `p747`'s `T401` on a second, unrelated estate — which
promotes it from an observation to a **rule**: read `default_branch` from the search payload before any
`raw` fetch, always.

## T422 — 🔴 Both addresses the accessibility literature cites for the maths-accessibility layer are dead

`zorkow/speech-rule-engine` → **`422`**. `NSoiffer/MathCAT` → **`422`**. Both moved into organisations:
[`Speech-Rule-Engine/speech-rule-engine`](https://github.com/Speech-Rule-Engine/speech-rule-engine)
(Apache-2.0, `105★`) and [`daisy/MathCAT`](https://github.com/daisy/MathCAT) (MIT, `131★`, pushed
`2026-11-10`). 🔵 The author-named forms are what papers, blog posts and vendor docs cite, so a successor
researching this tier from the literature will write two `404`s into a client deliverable.
Also moved: `jbarlow83/OCRmyPDF` → [`ocrmypdf/OCRmyPDF`](https://github.com/ocrmypdf/OCRmyPDF);
`readium/readium-css` → [`readium/css`](https://github.com/readium/css).

## T423 — 🟢 The licence gradient runs along the *layer*, `18 / 18`, with zero crossovers — the cleanest confirmation of the seam this base has

- **Checkers, validators, format specifications (`10` rows): MIT ×`4`, Apache-2.0 ×`3`, BSD-3-Clause ×`3`. No copyleft.**
- **Assistive-technology runtime (`8` rows): LGPL-2.1, LGPL-3.0, GPL-2.0-or-later ×`2`, GPL-3.0 ×`3`, MPL-2.0 ×`2`. No permissive.**

🟢 **Fourth independent confirmation of `T360`, and the first with `0` crossovers in both directions.**
The reason is structural rather than cultural: a *checker* is sold to publishers and vendors who need to
embed it, so it is published permissively to get adopted; a *screen reader or braille translator* is built
by and for disability communities who use copyleft to keep it free for its users. 🔵 **The seam predicts
licences in tiers this base has not read yet**, and it yields a hard architectural rule — `P248`.

| **Remediate one document format** | `pdf accessibility remediation` | **`85`** |

| **Score a course inside the LMS** | `course accessibility checker lms` | **`1`** (`0★`) |

🟢 **The split is not about interest; it is about where the per-item cost and the human-review obligation
live.** Wiring `axe-core` to MCP is a weekend and costs nothing to run. Generating alt text for `40,000`
images, or captions for `6,000` lecture hours, has a real unit cost **and** cannot be shipped without human
review, because a confidently wrong alt text is worse for the student than none. 🔴 **That is precisely why
it is a services opportunity rather than a repository**, and it is the single most important commercial
reading in this pass.

[`bcgov/SIMS`](https://github.com/bcgov/SIMS) is the most credible thing in this register: a
province's production aid system, `Apache-2.0` (`11,358 B` `cfc7749b96f6`), *"new features released

accommodate regular changes in alignment with policy."* 🟢 **That is the right architecture.**
🔴 **The engine it names is not one Globant may ship.**

`sources/packages/backend/package.json` pins **`"@camunda8/sdk": "^8.8.18"`**. The core it drives,
[`camunda/camunda`](https://github.com/camunda/camunda) (`4,360★`, pushed the day of this pass), is
indexed **`NONE`** and has **no grant at `6` probed root paths**. The licence is at a non-probed
path, `licenses/CAMUNDA-LICENSE-1.0.txt` — **`3,559 B`, sha256₁₂ `bc6a88b51407`** — and it is the
**Camunda License Version 1.0**, whose grant is limited to:

> *"the Use in or for the purpose of Using the Software in Non-Production Environment. Non-Production
> Environment means a setting in which the Software is used for development, staging…"*

🔴 **Source-available, non-production only.** Parts are Apache-2.0 and the README enumerates them;
the engine is not among them.

🔴 **And the escape hatch is rusting.** [`camunda/camunda-bpm-platform`](https://github.com/camunda/camunda-bpm-platform)
— Camunda 7, genuinely `Apache-2.0`, `4,260★` — was **last pushed `2025-11-04`, twelve months before
this pass.**

🟢 **The permissive replacements exist, are larger, and were byte-read this pass:**
[`Activiti/Activiti`](https://github.com/Activiti/Activiti) (`Apache-2.0` `11,358 B`
`cfc7749b96f6`, `10,554★`, pushed `2026-11-10`),
[`flowable/flowable-engine`](https://github.com/flowable/flowable-engine) (`Apache-2.0`, same
digest, `9,642★`, pushed `2026-11-04`) and, for decision tables specifically,

`2026-11-10`). `P243` makes the substitution a pre-flight step rather than a migration.

⚠️ **Read this finding the right way: it is not a defect in SIMS.** A provincial ministry buying a
Camunda 8 licence is doing nothing wrong. The defect appears only when a systems integrator copies
the architecture of a published public-sector repository **and inherits its commercial
dependencies without reading them.**

## T412 — 🔴 Two MIT payloads in one pass carry no title block at all, so this base's "classify from the title block" method fails `2 / 31` — and the corrected discriminator is the operative clause

This base reports its licence reads as *"`n / n` classified from the title block"* (`36 / 37` at
`p747`, `26 / 26` at `p746`). 🔴 **`p748` scores `29 / 31`, and both failures are the same shape:**

| Repository | Index | Payload | First line | Classified by |
|---|---|--:|---|---|
| [`PolicyEngine/policyengine-taxsim`](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-taxsim) | `MIT` | `1,060 B` `ff117700ce78` | `Copyright 2024 PolicyEngine` | operative clause |
| [`gorules/zen`](https://github.com/gorules/zen) | `MIT` | `1,057 B` `2493262dd0c0` | `Copyright 2023 GoRules.io` | operative clause |

**Neither payload contains the string `MIT License` anywhere.** Both open on the copyright line and
go straight into the grant. A title-block classifier returns `UNRECOGNISED` on both — and an
`UNRECOGNISED` verdict on a permissive payload is the expensive direction of error, because it
pushes a usable repository into the refusal table.

🟢 **The repair, and it is one string:** classify MIT from the operative clause
**`Permission is hereby granted, free of charge`**, which is present and byte-stable in both.
⚠️ **Second trap, and it will bite a `grep`:** both payloads use **typographic quotes** —
`(the “Software”)`, `U+201C`/`U+201D` — not ASCII `"`. A pattern written with ASCII quotes matches
neither. Added to `P240` as check `8`.

🔵 **Scope stated honestly:** `1,057–1,069 B` is the MIT size band, so the *size* channel already
flagged both correctly. The finding is that the base's **primary** channel is the fragile one, and
the cheap corroborator was sitting next to it unused.

licence** (`0` matches for `licen[cs]e|AGPL|GPL|copyright`).

🟢 **The licence statement exists, in a channel this base has never read:** the Python packaging
metadata.

```
"License :: OSI Approved :: GNU Affero General Public License v3"
```

That is a **PyPI trove classifier** in the project's packaging config — a *declaration* of a grant,

| Phi-3.5-mini-instruct | english_rules | `0.588` | `0.030` | `$432` | `0.020` |
| Phi-3.5-mini-instruct | **statute_ctx** | **`0.645`** | `0.018` | `$441` | `0.009` |

Handing Phi-3.5 the **verbatim CFR text** produces the best accuracy in the table (`0.645`) and a κ

agreement.** Anyone evaluating an aid agent on accuracy alone will buy this. **Score κ, or score
nothing.**

not shown to be peer-reviewed. 🔴 **This does NOT measure frontier models, and it must not be
quoted as "LLMs cannot do eligibility."** What it supports is narrower and still decisive for
architecture: **a small model asked to *be* the determination is not fit for the purpose, and the
honest architecture puts the number in a deterministic engine.** `P241`.

## T416 — 🟢 Statutory churn in an eligibility register is measurable, and it is `33 / 199` fixtures in one year — `3` eligibility flips and `30` amount changes

From the same bundle's `results/quarterly-diff.json`, 2025 → 2026 parameter year:

| Outcome | Fixtures |
|---|--:|
| Unchanged | `166` |
| **Amount changed, eligibility same** | **`30`** |
| **Eligibility flipped** | **`3`** |
| Total | `199` |

🟢 **`16.6%` of cases change answer in a single parameter year, and the split is the useful part:**
eligibility is comparatively stable (`1.5%` flip) while **the money moves (`15.1%`)**. A
determination cached, fine-tuned into weights, or hard-coded in application logic is wrong for one
case in six within a year — and wrong *quietly*, because the eligible/ineligible headline still
matches.

🔵 **This is the strongest available argument for the `P242` architecture** — rules as versioned
data in an engine, parameters dated, the agent explaining rather than computing — and it is the
`P245` regression gate: re-run the fixture suite on every parameter release and diff, which is
exactly what the bundle's `quarterly_diff.py` does.

⚠️ **Scope:** US federal programmes, `6` of them, one year-over-year step. The *mechanism*
(annual indexation moves amounts, statute moves eligibility) is general; the `16.6%` is not a
constant and should be re-measured per jurisdiction.

## T408 — 🔴 This base's existence-probe chain has a second hole, it is one filename wide, and it fails on exactly the population most likely to be refused

`p747`'s own URL verification scored [`apereo/mod_auth_cas`](https://github.com/apereo/mod_auth_cas)
**dead** — `404` on all four links of the standing chain (`README.md` → `readme.md` → `README.rst`
→ `LICENSE`, the case-ordered form repaired at `724-I`). 🟢 **It is alive:** the search index
returns `count=1`, `150★`, `default_branch=master`, pushed `2026-05-27`, and the raw channel serves
`master/README` (**no extension**) and `master/configure.ac` with `200`.

| Probe | Result |
|---|--:|
| `master/README.md` | `404` |
| `master/README` | **`200`** |
| `master/configure.ac` | **`200`** |
| `HEAD/README` | **`200`** |

🔴 **The hole is `README` with no extension, and the correlation is the dangerous part.** The
chain's fourth link is `LICENSE`, so an extensionless `README` is only fatal when the repository
*also* has no root grant — which is precisely the **ungranted** population. 🔵 **So the probe
fails hardest on the repositories this base most needs to classify, and it converts an honest
`T302` "no grant at `7` probed paths" refusal into a false "dead address" claim.** `p745`'s `T375`
found this chain had "a hole one token wide"; this is a second, independent one.

🟢 **The repair is one link:** `README.md` → `readme.md` → `README.rst` → **`README`** →
`LICENSE`. Added as check `7` in `P240`. ⚠️ **And the liveness verdict of record for
`apereo/mod_auth_cas` is ALIVE and UNGRANTED** — its refusal on `agents/top.md` stands on the
grant absence, not on liveness.

## T396 — 🔴 The identity provider that most of global research-and-education runs is not on GitHub and is unreachable from this pipeline, which is why `746` passes never saw it

**Shibboleth** is the IdP behind InCommon, eduGAIN, the UK Access Management Federation, AAF,
GakuNin and most of the national federations this base has now enumerated. It has **`0` mentions
across every live shelf**. That was never an oversight:

| Probe | Result |
|---|---|
| `gh api -X GET search/repositories -f q='org:shibboleth'` | **`422`** — the `T359` *"not a canonical current address"* state |
| `org:Shibboleth` (case variant) | **`422`** |
| `curl -L https://www.shibboleth.net/` | **proxy `CONNECT` → `403`** |
| `curl -L https://git.shibboleth.net/` | **proxy `CONNECT` → `403`** |
| `curl -L https://shibboleth.atlassian.net/wiki/…` | **proxy `CONNECT` → `403`** |
| `shibboleth-identity-provider` (keyword, sorted by stars) | `Unicon/shibboleth-idp-dockerized` `109★` Apache-2.0 **pushed 2020-01-11**; `uchicago/shibboleth-oidc` `82★` Apache-2.0 **pushed 2020-10-13** |

🔴 **The project's source lives on its own Git service, which this environment's network policy does
not reach, and GitHub holds only third-party wrappers that stopped five to six years ago.**
🔵 **Three things follow, and the third is the valuable one.** First, this base's instrument is
GitHub-shaped, so anything off-GitHub is structurally invisible to it — `T396` is the first finding
to name that boundary explicitly. Second, **the absence of a project from these shelves is not
evidence about the project.** Third, and operationally: **an engagement that must evaluate or extend
Shibboleth cannot be served from this pipeline** and needs a channel that reaches
`git.shibboleth.net`. That is a better answer to give a client than silence.

🟢 **What this base *can* serve instead, all verified this pass:** the SAML libraries
(`IdentityPython/pysaml2`, Apache-2.0), the protocol proxy (`SATOSA`, Apache-2.0), the metadata
aggregator (`pyFF`, BSD-2-Clause), the alternative IdP (`simplesamlphp`, LGPL-2.1), the entitlement
authority (`Internet2/grouper`, Apache-2.0) and the deployable federation platform (`OpenConext`,
Apache-2.0).

[`REFEDS/eduperson`](https://github.com/REFEDS/eduperson) holds the **eduPerson** object class and
schema files — `eduPersonPrincipalName`, `eduPersonTargetedID`, `eduPersonEntitlement`, the
attributes an IdP actually asserts about a student. The GitHub index says **`NOASSERTION`**. The
payload is **`Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International`** (`20,848 B`, sha256₁₂
`9e502ba75fd0`).

🔴 **NonCommercial, on the schema, from the body that defines it.** `p744`'s `T372` found an
`MIT`-indexed repository at `2,285★` shipping `CC BY-NC-SA 4.0` inside itself; this is the same
defect one layer more consequential, because **the artefact is a standard rather than a tool.**

🟢 **The operational rule, and it is narrow enough to follow:** *reference* the eduPerson
specification by attribute name — attribute names are not copyrightable — and **never vendor the
schema files, LDIF or object-class definitions into a client deliverable.** Enforced as a refusal in
`P237`. 🔵 **And note the shape of the surrounding estate:** `org:refeds` is `5` repositories and
`4 / 5` are `NOASSERTION` documents. The standards layer of this tier is the **least** clearly
licensed part of it, which inverts `p745`'s `T381` (where the standards body was the permissive one).

## T398 — 🔴 `p746`'s `END OF TERMS AND CONDITIONS` discriminator fails as a presence test on its first reuse, and the corrected rule is narrower

`p746` declared `T391`: an Apache-2.0 payload can be the licence concatenated with itself, and the
discriminator is `grep -c 'END OF TERMS AND CONDITIONS'`. 🔴 **Used as a test for *whether* a payload
is Apache-2.0, it returns a false negative.**

[`OpenConext/Stepup-saml-bundle`](https://github.com/OpenConext/Stepup-saml-bundle): index
`Apache-2.0`, payload `10,140 B`, digest `4cd13f7a31e9`, title block *"Apache License / Version 2.0,
January 2004"*, body complete through clause 9 ("Accepting Warranty or Additional Liability") — and
**no `END OF TERMS AND CONDITIONS` line and no appendix at all.** `EOT = 0`.

| Rule | Status after `p747` |
|---|---|
| `EOT ≥ 2` ⇒ the payload contains the licence more than once | 🟢 **Holds.** `T391`'s actual finding |
| `EOT = 1` ⇒ canonical single Apache-2.0 | 🟢 Holds on `33` of this pass's Apache payloads |
| `EOT = 0` ⇒ not Apache-2.0 | 🔴 **FALSE.** `1` counter-example at `10,140 B` |

🟢 **Classification stays with the title block, which was `36 / 37` this pass.** The grep is a
*doubling* detector and nothing else. 🔵 **This is the third consecutive pass in which the previous
pass's newest instrument needed narrowing on first use** (`p745`'s `T374` → `p746`'s `T388`;
`p746`'s `T391` → this; `p746`'s `T392` → `T400`). **A finding declared in the pass that discovered
it has not yet been tested; `p748` should treat `T396`–`T407` the same way.**

## T399 — 🔴 A file named `LICENSE` can be a pointer rather than a grant, and the real terms can require deploying the software to read

[`GEANT/CAT`](https://github.com/GEANT/CAT) — `124★`, the eduroam **Configuration Assistant Tool**,
the generator behind per-institution eduroam installers across Europe. Index: **`NOASSERTION`**.
`LICENSE`: **`1,095 B`**, digest `e772049431f9`, and it opens `/*` — it is a **C comment block**. It
records GÉANT's copyright and its EU framework-programme grant numbers (GN3 `238875`, GN3plus
`605243`, GN4-1 `691567`, GN4-2 `731122`), its Amsterdam Chamber of Commerce registration, and then:

> *"License: see the `web/copyright.inc.php` file in the file structure or
> `<base_url>/copyright.php` after deploying the software"*

🟢 **Resolved by a second fetch** — `web/copyright.inc.php` returns `200` on the raw channel
(`copyright.php` at the root returns `404`). The terms are a **bespoke licence governed by English
copyright law**: derivative works must be licensed under the same licence, no endorsement using
GÉANT's name or marks, and explicitly **"No patent licence is granted"** beyond one narrow claim set.

🔴 **Three gates score this wrongly and the third is this base's own.** The search index reports
nothing. A `LICENSE`-exists probe reports *granted*. **A probe that reads the first line and
pattern-matches `Copyright (c)` reports a BSD-family permissive grant** — because that is exactly
what the top of this file looks like. 🟢 **The discriminator is cheap:** a payload whose first
non-blank character is `/*`, `#`, `<!--` or `//` is a **source header**, not a licence, and the word
`License:` followed by a path is a **deferral**. Wired into `P234`'s pre-flight as a fourth grep.
⚠️ **Disposition: refused for build-on work**, filed on `verticals/solutions.md` for the market map
and the integration surface only.

## T400 — 🔴 `p746`'s publisher-digest control does not generalise: cross-publisher byte-identity is the *norm* for Apache-2.0

`p746` declared `T392`: a repeated licence digest identifies a publisher's canonical payload. 🔴 **On
`37` payloads from `19` publishers, the same digests cross publisher boundaries freely.**

| Digest | Size | Publishers carrying it |
|---|--:|---|
| `58d1e17ffe51` | `11,357 B` | **`IdentityPython`, `Internet2`, `REANNZ`, `CSCfi`, `babs`** — five unrelated |
| `43070e2d4e53` | `11,356 B` | `casdoor`, `OpenConext` |
| `c5accbbd8546` | `11,356 B` | `Unicon`, `uchicago` |
| `ef777cb1e5f4` | `10,177 B` | `IdentityPython` ×2 (`SATOSA`, `pyop`) — **within** one publisher |
| `0cec06e0e55f` | `10,173 B` | `OpenConext` ×2 (`engineblock`, `pdp`) — **within** one publisher |

🟢 **Corrected statement:** *within* one publisher, a repeated digest is evidence of a canonical
payload and is useful for `P210`-style duplicate detection. *Across* publishers it is evidence of
nothing but the SPDX reference text, which thousands of projects copy byte-for-byte. 🔴 **The failure
mode `p746` was one step away from:** inferring common authorship, or a fork relationship, from a
shared digest. `babs/mcp-auth-proxy` and `CSCfi/shibboleth-idp-oidc-extension` share a digest and
have nothing whatever to do with each other.

🔵 **And `T383` is re-confirmed on a fifth licence family.** **Eight** distinct byte sizes read this
pass — `10,140`, `10,173`, `10,177`, `10,758`, `11,323`, `11,337`, `11,356`, `11,357 B` — **all
classify Apache-2.0 from the title block.** Size is not identity; the title block is.

| `CSCfi/shibboleth-idp-oidc-extension` | **`maint-1`** | 🟢 Apache-2.0, `LICENSE.txt`, `11,357 B` |
| `incommon/InCatalog` | **`develop`** | 🟢 Apache-2.0, `11,357 B` |

🔴 **`4` of `37` (`11%`) — and a probe hard-coded to `main`/`master` scores every one of them
grant-absent**, which would have produced four false refusals in a tier that is overwhelmingly
permissive. 🔵 **The institutional-publisher correlation is worth naming:** all four are university,
NREN or consortium publishers running long-lived maintenance branches, which is precisely the
population this base now spends most of its passes in. 🟢 **Standing procedure (`P240`): take
`default_branch` from the search index on every probe; never assume, and never use `HEAD` as a
stand-in on a repository whose metadata you already hold.**

## T404 — 🟢 National federation code crosses regions and keeps its grant: Japan's discovery service is a maintained Swiss derivative, and the index calls it `NOASSERTION`

[`gakunin/gakunin-ds`](https://github.com/gakunin/gakunin-ds) is the discovery service of **GakuNin**,
Japan's national academic access-management federation, operated by NII. Index: `NOASSERTION`. Pushed
**`2026-10-22`**. The payload (`3,329 B`, digest `c8c7ba659fa2`) opens:

> *"License note for the SWITCHwayf code — Copyright (c) 2012, SWITCH – Serving Swiss Universities.
> All rights reserved."*

…and continues as a textbook **BSD-3-Clause** (three conditions, non-endorsement clause naming
SWITCH). 🟢 **So the APAC national service is a fourteen-year-lived derivative of the EMEA national
service, still carrying the Swiss NREN's grant, actively maintained, and invisible to the index.**

🔵 **Two consequences for engagement work.** First, **NREN code is a reuse network rather than a set
of national silos** — the same artefact appears in Switzerland, Japan and (via
`REANNZ/federationregistry2-Tuakiri`, the AAF's registry deployed for New Zealand's Tuakiri)
Australia and New Zealand. A platform validated in one NREN is a credible proposal in another.
Second, 🔴 **the estate around it is mostly ungranted:** `org:GakuNin` is `5` repositories, `5 / 5`
indexed `NOASSERTION`, and of the two byte-probed, `gakunin/orthros-docs` (pushed `2026-11-06`) has
**no grant at `7` probed paths** while `gakunin-ds` has a clean BSD-3-Clause. **The ratio of
actively-pushed-to-clearly-licensed is the risk to raise in an APAC engagement**, and it is one
`curl` per repository to establish.

## T406 — 🟢 There is no ratified standard for what an AI agent presents as its identity, and higher education is the exposed sector — which is what makes this register commercial *now*

| Instrument | Status, late `2026` |
|---|---|
| **NIST CAISI** (Center for AI Standards and Innovation) **AI Agent Standards Initiative** | Opened **February 2026**; drafting in progress as of mid-2026 |
| **NIST NCCoE** | Concept paper published following the CAISI initiative |
| **Cloud Security Alliance**, agentic-identity guidance | Published **September 2026** |
| **OWASP Non-Human Identity Top 10** | Available and being used as the de-facto control set |
| **NIST CSF 2.0 `PR.AC-4`** (least privilege) | The control existing audits are mapped to |
| A ratified NHI/agent-identity standard | 🔴 **None.** Vendor platforms are shipping ahead of it, so *agent delegation* means something different in each one |

🔴 **Why education is the exposed sector rather than an average one:** an agent acting for a student
touches education records that are statutorily protected — FERPA in the United States, the EU AI
Act's Annex III education obligations from **2 Dec 2027**, and a dozen national equivalents this
base's `intel/policy-matrix.tsv` already tracks. **An agent with a service account has the
institution's authority; an agent with a delegated assertion has the student's.** The second is
defensible to a regulator and the first is not.

🟢 **What this base can now put behind that argument, all verified this pass:**
`babs/mcp-auth-proxy` (Apache-2.0) to make the agent an OAuth client rather than a credential
holder; `IdentityPython/SATOSA` (Apache-2.0) to bridge OAuth to the federation's SAML;
`Internet2/grouper` (Apache-2.0) as the entitlement source of truth;
`Internet2/comanage-registry` (Apache-2.0) as the register where a non-human identity gets a
**human owner, a purpose and an expiry** — the NHI Management Group's three requirements, satisfied
by a platform that has existed for a decade. `P235` and `P236`.

⚠️ **Sourcing note.** The standards-status rows above come from a CSA report, a CSO opinion piece, an
EdTech Magazine article and vendor blogs; the **NIST CAISI and NCCoE outputs are the primary sources
to track** and the vendor commentary should not be quoted to a client as fact.

## T407 — 🟢 The federation tier's licence gradient runs along the *language estate* rather than the layer, and the architectural rule falls straight out of it

`p745`'s `T381` found the assessment tier's gradient running **standards-permissive /
platform-copyleft**. This tier does not split that way at all.

| Estate | Payloads read | Verdict | Sizes |
|---|--:|---|---|
| **Python** — `IdentityPython`: `pysaml2`, `SATOSA`, `djangosaml2`, `pyop` | `4 / 4` | 🟢 **Apache-2.0** | `10,758` · `10,177` · `11,357` · `10,177 B` |
| **PHP** — `simplesamlphp`: core, `saml2` | `2 / 2` | ⚠️ **LGPL-2.1** | `24,487` · `24,459 B` |
| **PHP module layer** — `simplesamlphp-module-oidc` | `1 / 1` | 🟢 **MIT** (RedIRIS, Spain) | `1,250 B` |
| **Java** — `apereo` (held from `p736`) | — | 🟢 Apache-2.0 | — |
| **Platform** — `OpenConext`, `Internet2`, `incommon`, `REANNZ` | `7 / 7` | 🟢 Apache-2.0 | `10,140`–`11,357 B` |
| **Standards** — `REFEDS`, `SeamlessAccess` | `1` read, `7` indexed | 🔴 **`CC BY-NC-SA 4.0`** / `NOASSERTION` | `20,848 B` |

🟢 **The rule, and it is architectural rather than legal:** **write the Globant-owned components in
Python against `SATOSA` and `pysaml2`, and integrate with SimpleSAMLphp across its *module*
interface rather than forking its core.** LGPL-2.1 at the library level means a module links
cleanly and a fork of core carries the copyleft into the deliverable. 🔵 **The module layer proves
the route exists:** `simplesamlphp-module-oidc` is **MIT inside an LGPL-2.1 publisher** — RedIRIS
wrote an OIDC OP for SimpleSAMLphp without inheriting its licence, which is exactly the shape a
Globant module should take. 🔴 **And the inversion against `T381` is the part to carry forward:** in
this tier the **standards layer is the least clearly licensed** (`REFEDS` `4 / 5` `NOASSERTION`,
eduPerson NonCommercial) while the **platforms are permissive** — the opposite of the assessment
tier, so the posture must be re-derived per tier and never assumed. `P239`.
