## T388 — 🔴 `T374` is NOT satisfiable in this session: the whole `api.github.com/repos/` namespace is gated, so tree denominators and commit-record placement are both unavailable

`p745` published compliant grant-absences **with tree denominators** (`669` tree entries, `18`
distinct grants) and placed a row as **North America** from *"the commit record"*, citing a working
`git` tree channel as `T374` — and explicitly recorded that `T302`'s contrary conclusion had been
"about HTTP rather than about the environment".

🔴 **In this session the channel is closed, on `2 / 2` controls, and it fails identically for both
callers:**

| Channel | Call | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Authenticated | `gh api repos/dhis2-metadata/EMIS_AGG/git/trees/HEAD?recursive=1` | 🔴 session-gate message: *"GitHub access to this repository is not enabled for this session"* |
| Unauthenticated | `curl https://api.github.com/repos/dhis2/dhis2-emis-docs/git/trees/HEAD?recursive=1` | 🔴 **the same session-gate message** — including for a repository whose **bytes the raw channel serves happily** |
| Archive | `curl https://codeload.github.com/dhis2-metadata/EMIS_AGG/tar.gz/refs/heads/master` | 🔴 `403`, `378 B` body |

🔵 **The discriminating detail: the gate is not about whether the repository exists or is public.**
`dhis2/dhis2-emis-docs` returns a full `BSD-3-Clause` payload over
`raw.githubusercontent.com` in the same minute that `api.github.com/repos/…` refuses to describe it.
**It is a namespace gate, not a liveness signal** — which is exactly the shape of `T289`, now
established for the whole `repos/` namespace and for the unauthenticated caller too.

🟢 **Consequences, stated so the next pass does not re-derive them:**
1. **Grant-absence verdicts revert to `T302`'s honest negative** — *"no grant at `N` probed paths"* —
   and **must not claim a denominator.** This pass recorded `2` such absences that way.
2. **Commit-record placement is unavailable.** `T378` placement must come from a **payload holder
   line** (strongest), **README text**, or a **publishing programme**; never from a commit e-mail.
3. 🔴 **`p745`'s `669`-entry and `18`-grant figures cannot be reproduced here and should not be
   re-quoted to a client without a fresh read.** Whether the environment changed or the figures came
   from elsewhere is undecidable from inside this session, and that uncertainty is the finding.

🔵 **What *is* confirmed working, re-controlled this pass:** `gh api -X GET search/repositories`
(full metadata, `T359`/`T310`) and `raw.githubusercontent.com/{owner}/{repo}/HEAD/{path}`
(`200` alive / `404` absent, `2 / 2`). **Metadata from search, bytes from raw — and nothing from
`repos/`.**

**`7 / 7`, zero crossovers, one publisher.** `p742` found this seam on `eol-uchile` (xblock vs theme)
and again on `edukors_graph`; this is the third independent confirmation and the first where the
*whole* publisher was swept rather than a sample.

🔵 **Why this is now a rule rather than a correlation.** Three publishers, three countries, three
technology stacks, same boundary: **the thing you *run* is copyleft and the thing you *learn from*
is permissive.** The mechanism is not mysterious — a funder protects the service it operates and
releases the research it wants adopted. 🟢 **Operationally: ask "which layer is this?" before
"who published this?", and read the licence of the subtree you will actually ship.** `P234`.

## T390 — 🔴 A `NOASSERTION` index value can conceal an actively proprietary grant, and the most complete artefact in a tier is where it bit

[`winterop-com/dhis2w`](https://github.com/winterop-com/dhis2w) and
[`winterop-com/dhis2w-mcp`](https://github.com/winterop-com/dhis2w-mcp) are indexed
**`NOASSERTION`**. The payload (`785 B`, sha256₁₂ `3d2034562ea8`, **byte-identical across both**,
© *2026 Morten Olav Hansen*) reads:

> *"No license, express or implied, is granted to use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute,
> sublicense, or sell copies of this software or its derivatives. The source is published for
> reference only. Any use beyond reading requires written permission from the copyright holder."*

🔴 **This is worse than `T302`'s honest negative and worse than `P741-B`'s dangling reference,
because `NOASSERTION` reads as *"licence not detected, probably fine"* while the text actively
forbids use.** `P739-A` established that the index is wrong in both directions about the licence
*family*; this is a third direction — **the index has no vocabulary for "source-available but
all rights reserved"**, and files it under the same value it uses for an unparseable `MIT`.

⚠️ **And the cost is real rather than theoretical:** these two repositories are the **most
feature-complete** DHIS2 agent artefacts this pass found — client, CLI, MCP server and browser
automation in one toolkit — published by a developer whose name appears on the DHIS2 estate itself.
**The best tool in the tier is the one Globant may not build on.** 🟢 **Procedure: treat
`NOASSERTION` as "unknown, read the bytes", never as "permissive by default"** — and read them
*before* building a recipe around the artefact, not after.

## T391 — 🟢 An `Apache-2.0` payload can be the licence concatenated with itself, and the discriminator is one `grep`

[`unicef/giga-open-cost-model`](https://github.com/unicef/giga-open-cost-model) serves
**`22,713 B`** of `Apache-2.0` against the steward's `11,358 B` — **roughly double**, and far
outside the **`1,184 B`** spread that `693-G` and `p739` established across every Apache payload
this base had read (`10,173`–`11,357 B`).

🔴 **It is not a variant and it has no added clause.** The file contains **`2` occurrences of
`END OF TERMS AND CONDITIONS`** (lines `176`, `377`) and **`8` of `Apache License`**: the licence is
duplicated in place.

🟢 **Rule, and it costs nothing — it belongs beside `P742-C`'s conflict-marker check on every
grant read:**

```
grep -c 'END OF TERMS AND CONDITIONS'   # > 1  =>  concatenated payload, not an altered one
```

🔵 **Why it matters practically:** a size heuristic — the thing a reader reaches for first — files
`22,713 B` as *"modified Apache, find the extra clause"* and sends them hunting for a restriction
that does not exist. The operative terms here are the stock terms, **twice**.

## T379 — 🔴 This base has been optimising the wrong number: novelty and relevance came apart by a factor of ten, and no pass before this one measured them separately

`p744` closed by celebrating a rediscovery rate of `0 / 15`, and `p741` was marked down for `44%`.
Both numbers describe **novelty** — is this address already on a shelf or in the ledger. `p745` ran
`10` legs in a new register and measured novelty the same way: **`102 / 215` candidate addresses
novel (`47%`)**, which by the standing scoreboard is a strong pass.

🔴 **Almost none of it was usable.** Of the `102` novel addresses, the top of the ranking is
`trimstray/test-your-sysadmin-skills` (`11,902★`, Linux sysadmin interview questions),
`miss-mumu/developer2gwy` (`11,500★`, a Chinese civil-service exam guide),
`walidshaari/Kubernetes-Certified-Administrator` (`4,455★`) and
`noraj/OSCP-Exam-Report-Template-Markdown` (`4,222★`). **After filtering for on-topic, `8` of the
`102` were worth a licence read.** The novelty rate was `47%`; the *yield* rate was `~8%`.

🔵 **The correction is to the scoreboard, not to the method.** A novel address is cheap to
recognise and tells you only that this base has not seen it. Relevance is the expensive question
and it is the one that decides whether a row gets written. **Both numbers should be published from
now on, and a pass that reports only the first is reporting the easy half.** `p745` publishes
`47% novel / 8% yield` and considers the second number the honest one.

## T381 — 🟢 The assessment tier's licence gradient runs the *opposite* way to the scholarly tier's, and the rule that falls out is architectural

`T364` (p743) recorded an inversion inside one publisher: Invenio's framework is MIT and Zenodo, the
famous instance built on it, is GPL-2.0. **In the assessment tier the inversion is tier-wide and it
runs by layer, not by publisher:**

- **The standards body is the permissive one.** `1EdTech` — which *owns* QTI, LTI, OneRoster, Open
  Badges and CASE — publishes Apache-2.0 and MIT across its implementation libraries
  (`lti-1-3-php-library`, `basiclti-util-java`, `openbadges-validator-core`, `OpenCASE`,
  `cert-schema` MIT `1,096 B` `06d87bf42a0a`).
- **A commercial vendor is permissive too.** `Learnosity` publishes Apache-2.0 SDKs in `7`
  languages — its entire integration surface, under a licence a studio can build on.
- **Every deployable implementation is copyleft.** TAO is GPL-2.0 across `18 / 20` repositories,
  the SEB estate is MPL-2.0, and anything that enters Moodle is GPL-3.0 by force.

🔵 **So the architectural rule is: build on the spec, integrate with the platform.** The permissive
artefacts in this tier are exactly the ones that describe an *interface* — and an interface is what
a studio wants to own anyway, because it is what survives the client changing LMS. `P229` prices it.

## T382 — 🔴 A `149★` platform publishes its only grant at `Resources/LICENCE`, and the two files in it named `LICENSE` belong to somebody else

[`SafeExamBrowser/seb-mac`](https://github.com/SafeExamBrowser/seb-mac) — Safe Exam Browser for
macOS and iOS, `149★`, `69` forks, pushed `2026-11-09` — is indexed `NOASSERTION` and is **MPL-2.0**
(`16,726 B`, `3f3d9e0024b1`). Two of the shared probe's three documented traps fire on one path:
the payload is in a **subdirectory** (trap #2) and it is spelled **`LICENCE`** (trap #3).

🔴 **The part that is new, and that no previous pass has recorded, is the failure mode of the
obvious workaround.** The repository contains two files named exactly `LICENSE`:
`Pods/JitsiMeetSDK/LICENSE` (Apache-2.0, `558 B`) and
`SEB/QRCodeReaderViewController/LICENSE` (MIT, `1,089 B`) — **both vendored dependencies**. A sweep
that globs the tree for `LICENSE` and takes the first match does not abstain; it **asserts
Apache-2.0 or MIT for a Mozilla-licensed application**. That is strictly worse than the index's own
`NOASSERTION`, because it is confident.

🔵 **The control that survives is positional, not lexical:** a payload at depth > 1 under
`Pods/`, `vendor/`, `node_modules/` or `external/` is a *dependency's* grant until proven otherwise,
and a project's own grant is the one at the shallowest depth — whatever it is spelled. `P230` makes
this a step rather than an instinct.

## T383 — 🔴 Three AGPL-3.0 payloads at *exactly* `34,523 B`, two byte-identical and one not — the cleanest refutation of size-as-identity this base will get

`T313` and `T376` established that byte size cannot identify a licence. This pass produced the
limiting case, within one family, in one sitting:

| Repo | Path | Bytes | sha256₁₂ |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tesla-ce/core` | `LICENSE` | **`34,523`** | `8486a10c4393` |
| `aalramadan/PeerCheck` | `external/mubanal/LICENSE` | **`34,523`** | `8486a10c4393` |
| `i4s-htwk/PySeA-public` | `LICENSE.txt` | **`34,523`** | 🔴 **`0d96a4ff68ad`** |

**Same family, same byte count to the byte, three unrelated publishers — and the third file is not
the same file.** 🟢 Meanwhile the digest did its job in both directions: the first two *are*
byte-identical across unrelated publishers (canonical text confirmed), and
`Learnosity/learnosity-sdk-php`'s Apache-2.0 payload matched its own vendored copy inside
`learnosity-demos` at `4e3d4f2274df`.

The same pass also added a **fourth** AGPL-3.0 byte length (`uzh-bf/p8-automated-correction` at
`32,386 B`, against `34,280` / `34,520` / `34,523` already held), a **third** GPL-3.0 length
(`35,147 B`, against `35,141` / `35,149`), and an Apache-2.0 at `9,235 B` against a held set that
already spanned `682`–`11,565 B`. 🔵 **The band heuristic is not merely unreliable; it has no
width left.** Nothing but the digest should ever be published as identity.

## T384 — 🟢 `ACTION p744-A`'s second carry paid out on first use, and what it found was a repository disagreeing with itself

p744 told this pass to **read the notice, not only the canonical text**. Applied to
[`Learnosity/learnosity-sdk-php`](https://github.com/Learnosity/learnosity-sdk-php), the three
channels do not agree:

| Channel | Says |
|---|---|
| Root payload (`LICENSE.md`, `9,235 B`, `4e3d4f2274df`) | **Apache-2.0** |
| Packaging metadata (`composer.json` → `"license"`) | **Apache-2.0** |
| 🔴 Source headers, every file | **`Copyright (c) 2021 / 2023 / 2025 Learnosity, MIT License`** |

This is a **maintained, currently-released vendor SDK**, not an abandoned repository. Both grants
are permissive, so nothing here is unshippable — which is precisely why it is worth recording:
**the disagreement is invisible to every consequence-driven check.** Nobody notices, because
nothing breaks.

🔵 **The generalisation, and it is the useful part:** the notice is not a weaker copy of the
payload, it is an **independent assertion**, and the two can diverge in either direction. `T371`
found the notice carrying *more* than the payload (`-or-later`). `T384` finds it carrying
*something else entirely*. A verdict should name the channel it came from — `Apache-2.0 (payload,
packaging)` — rather than claiming the repository has a licence full stop.

## T385 — 🔴 A `2★` repository indexed `GPL-3.0` ships `18` grants, and two of them are AGPL-3.0

[`aalramadan/PeerCheck`](https://github.com/aalramadan/PeerCheck) (Kent State University, `669`
tree entries) carries GPL-3.0 at its root and **seventeen further licence payloads** under

(ACL, iDRAMA Lab ×4 at one digest `3a65b949f3e2`, OpenReview, HotCRP, and a test fixture),
BSD-3-Clause, MPL-2.0, Apache-2.0 and a Creative Commons text.

🔴 **The AGPL pair is the whole finding.** p744's `T372` found `CC BY-NC-SA` inside an MIT
repository, which blocks a *commercial* deliverable. AGPL-3.0 §13 is narrower and lands harder in
this industry: it reaches **hosted** software, and an AI marking service is hosted by definition.
A studio that vendors `external/` into a SaaS assessment product inherits a network-copyleft
obligation **from a `2★` repository whose badge says GPL-3.0**.

🔵 **And the shape repeats across the pass**, which is what makes it a rule rather than an anecdote:
`seb-mac` hides its own grant under vendored ones, `learnosity-demos` is MIT at root over Apache-2.0
beneath, `PeerCheck` is GPL-3.0 at root over AGPL-3.0 beneath. **Three of this pass's rows carry a
grant the index cannot see, and in all three cases the index is reporting depth-1 only.** `P230` is
the sweep.

p744 directed this pass at `org:oat-sa`, `org:learnosity`, `org:safeexambrowser` and the rest as

asserted an absence it had not measured, and the measurement was one `grep -F` away.

## T371 — 🔴 The `-or-later` arm of a copyleft grant lives in the *notice*, never in the canonical text, and the search index publishes the bare version

**The measurement.** Three repositories, three families, one pass:

| Repository | Canonical full text in tree | Where `-or-later` is declared | Index field |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Koha-Community/Koha` | `LICENSE` — GPL-3.0, `35,151 B`, digest `e79e9c8a0c85` | **`debian/copyright`**, `970 B`: `License: GPL-3+`, *"either version 3 of the License, or (at your option) any later version"* | `GPL-3.0` |
| `ckan/ckan` | none at root | **`LICENSE.txt`**, `2,504 B`: AGPL *"either version 3 … or (at your option) any later version"* | `NOASSERTION` |
| `openpreserve/jhove` | `COPYING` — LGPL-2.1, `26,419 B` | **`LICENSE`**, `880 B`: LGPL *"either version 2.1 … or (at your option) any later version"* | `NOASSERTION` |

**Why the canonical text cannot answer it.** The FSF's full texts are identical bytes whether a
project grants `-only` or `-or-later`; the choice is made in the *notice the project writes about*
the text. So a pass that reads only `LICENSE`/`COPYING` is structurally unable to see the arm, and
a pass that trusts the index gets the bare version in `1 / 3` cases and `NOASSERTION` in `2 / 3`.

**Why a client pays for the difference.** `-or-later` lets the client relicense the work forward
onto FSF terms not yet written; `-only` freezes it. For a deliverable with a ten-year institutional
life that is a real option, and it is also the one copyleft question a procurement lawyer asks
first.

🔧 **Rule for later passes:** after reading the root payload, read the **notice** — and in a
Debian-packaged project read `debian/copyright`, where the arm is sometimes declared **and nowhere
else**. 🔴 **And do not match the arm by exact phrase:** jhove's own notice misspells its licence
(*"GNU **Lessor** General Public License"*), so a notice-only repository with that typo is
unplaceable by phrase anchoring.

**The specimen.** [`poco-ai/Agentero`](https://github.com/poco-ai/Agentero) — `2,285★`, `135`
forks, pushed `2026-11-10`, index field `MIT`, and the root payload **is** MIT
(`1,064 B`, digest `f2b7f0cc6fb1`, holder `poco-ai`). Three further grants in the tree:

| Path | Bytes | Digest | Family | Holder |
|---|--:|---|---|---|
| `templates/vault/.agents/skills/deep-research/LICENSE` | **1,028** | `b35c958b7972` | 🔴 **CC BY-NC-SA 4.0** | Yuyu Luo (methodology) and contributors |
| `templates/vault/.agents/skills/idea-evaluator/LICENSE` | **1,028** | `b35c958b7972` | 🔴 **CC BY-NC-SA 4.0** | *(same payload, byte-identical)* |
| `templates/vault/.agents/skills/research-paper-writing/LICENSE` | 1,066 | `34415967a8be` | 🟢 MIT | **Master-cai** — a third party |

**The exposure, stated as a studio would hit it.** `templates/vault/` is the directory a team
copies to stand the agent up for a client. Two of its three skills forbid commercial use. The
repository's index field, its README and its root grant all say MIT; nothing in the places a
reviewer looks says otherwise.

🔴 **And the size prior points the wrong way.** The `11` MIT payloads read this pass span
`1,061–1,080 B`. The **NonCommercial** payload is `1,028 B` — *below the entire MIT range* — so a
heuristic of "small payload ⇒ permissive notice" files it as MIT-ish. This is `T313`'s finding at a
sharper angle: size is not merely a weak discriminator, it is **anti-correlated** here.

🔵 Related, same pass, opposite sign: `Galaxy-Dawn/claude-scholar` (`6,025★`) bundles skills too,
and its three payloads are MIT + Apache-2.0 + Apache-2.0 — **permissive end to end**. The pattern
is not "bundled skills are dangerous"; it is **"bundled skills are separately licensed, so read
them."**

|---|--:|---|---|---|
| [`54yyyu/zotero-mcp`](https://github.com/54yyyu/zotero-mcp) | **5,841** | `MIT` | 🟢 MIT, `1,080 B` | 🔴 **`plugin/LICENSE` — AGPL-3.0, `34,524 B`, digest `8d56b405468a`** |
| [`yilewang/llm-for-zotero`](https://github.com/yilewang/llm-for-zotero) | **3,541** | `AGPL-3.0` | 🔴 AGPL-3.0, `34,520 B` | 🟢 **`packages/claude-bridge/` ships BOTH `LICENSE` (AGPL-3.0) and `LICENSE-MIT` (`1,069 B`) — a dual grant** |

**Why both repositories are shaped this way, and why the tier will keep producing it.** Zotero
itself is AGPL-3.0. Anything that runs *inside* Zotero as a plugin inherits that posture; anything
that talks to Zotero *over an API* — an MCP server — does not. So these projects are genuinely two
things in one tree, and the licence boundary sits exactly on the architectural boundary.

🔧 **Rule:** on this tier, **read the subtree you intend to ship, not the repository.** `3 / 4` of
the high-star rows filed to `agents/top.md` this pass have a different answer at the root than at
the directory a studio would vendor. 🔵 And note the second row is the *useful* direction: the
index is **pessimistic**, and a pass that trusted `AGPL-3.0` would have refused a component that is
available under MIT.

the digest is the identity. Size alone is a presentation detail.

## T377 — 🟢 Three `NOASSERTION` platforms are permissive and one is strong copyleft, because all four grant by *short-form notice* — and a fifth is neither

`T313` established that Apache-2.0-by-notice reads as `NOASSERTION`. This pass measures the
population effect on the **platform** shelf, where the field decides whether a studio can host a
fork:

| Repository | Index | Bytes | Direction |
|---|---|---|---|
| `projectblacklight/blacklight` `797★` | `NOASSERTION` | **Apache-2.0**, `788 B` — holders UVa + Stanford + Johns Hopkins + Data Curation Experts | 🟢 cheaper than the index implies |
| `archivesspace/archivesspace` `448★` | `NOASSERTION` | **ECL-2.0**, `748 B` — holders NYU + UC Regents + U Illinois | 🟢 cheaper |
| `openpreserve/fido` `160★` | `NOASSERTION` | **Apache-2.0**, `616 B` — the smallest complete grant read this pass | 🟢 cheaper |
| `ckan/ckan` `5,153★` | `NOASSERTION` | **AGPL-3.0-or-later**, `2,504 B` | 🔴 **dearer** — and this is the one that matters, because a hosted fork triggers the network clause |

⚠️ **The fifth is the one a human would get wrong where the index gets it right.**
`ORCID/orcid-model` indexes `NOASSERTION` and is **"ORCID MIT-Style License (MIT)"**, `1,669 B`,
digest `3eaeaa9ffbef`: MIT's grant clause, plus **three** terms MIT does not have —
(1) the grant **excludes** orcid.org branding and *"look and feel"*; (2) a **trademark clause**
forbids using the ORCID name, mark or logo to suggest affiliation; (3) attribution requires **the
full licence text or a link**, not the notice. 🔴 **Do not write "MIT" for it in a client's
dependency report.**

🔵 **The generalisation worth carrying:** `NOASSERTION` is not a signal about permissiveness in
either direction. It means *"this payload is not one of GitHub's canonical texts"* — which is true
of every short-form notice and of every bespoke grant, and those two classes point opposite ways.

## T368 — 🔴 Two ways a valid grant still fails to answer the question a client's counsel asks

**1. A grant that names no holder.** [`rdmorganiser/rdmo`](https://github.com/rdmorganiser/rdmo) (`137★`, Apache-2.0, byte-canonical) ships the appendix **unfilled**: `Copyright [yyyy] [name of copyright owner]`. The grant is complete and the attribution is absent, so **the row must be placed on its publisher, not its payload** — here the German DFG/NFDI programme. Any region or ownership cell derived from this payload alone would be derived from a template.

**2. A grant asserted by notice, with the terms not shipped.** [`lareferencia/dspace-stats-collector`](https://github.com/lareferencia/dspace-stats-collector) carries a `1,565 B` `LICENSE` that names *GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE Version 3*, states the standard *"either version 3 of the License, or (at your option) any later version"* notice under `© (C) 2019 LA Referencia` — and then pastes the GPL's own **"how to apply"** boilerplate instead of the licence body. Against GPL-3.0's `~35,145 B` of canonical text this is `4.5 %` of the document.

🟢 **The `p738` gate classifies both correctly** (`Apache-2.0`; `GPL-3.0`) because it decides on the family-name line and the operative clause, never on size — `1,565 B` would defeat any byte-band heuristic. 🔴 **But the index reports `NOASSERTION` for the second one**, which is the third index correction of this pass.

## T358 — 🔴 A licence file can ship unresolved git merge-conflict markers, assert two copyright holders at once, and still be reported clean by the index

**Subject:** [`0xnavarro/ia-para-todos`](https://github.com/0xnavarro/ia-para-todos), `26★`, Apache-2.0 per the index, `LICENSE` of **`11,471 B`**, sha256₁₂ `81fd0ede357d`.

🟢 **Adjudicated against the steward's own text**, which `T353` established is reachable in this session: `https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0.txt` → `200`, **`11,358 B`**, sha256₁₂ `cfc7749b96f6`.

The `113 B` excess is three conflict markers and an injected copyright line, sitting between `END OF TERMS AND CONDITIONS` and the appendix:

```
<<<<<<< HEAD
   Copyright 2024 0xnavarro - IA-PARA-TODOS
=======
   APPENDIX: How to apply the Apache License to your work.
   ...
   Copyright [yyyy] [name of copyright owner]
>>>>>>> 32db549aa17acfc812d4175d983a95945a02b728
```

🟢 **The delta reconciles exactly**, which is what separates this from an observation: `70 B` of marker lines `+ 44 B` injected copyright `− 1 B` removed leading blank `= 113 B`. **And the operative text is byte-canonical against the steward through `END OF TERMS AND CONDITIONS`** — line-by-line diff, zero differences.

🔴 **The defect is attribution, not grant.** The file asserts a real holder *and* the unfilled template, and does not say which governs. A conflict marker in a licence also means **a commit SHA is embedded in the licence file**.

🔴 **A fourth index-failure direction.** `T338`/`T341`/`T344` recorded the index being *wrong about the family*. Here it is **right about the family and blind to the document's condition** — the detector matched the operative body and stopped. 🟢 **Procedure, cheap and worth adding to any grant read: `grep -cE '^(<<<<<<<|=======|>>>>>>>)'` the payload.** It is one line and it catches a class no byte-count or family check can.

⚠️ **Disposition: not filed as a row.** The repository is a Spanish-language AI tutorial collection, last pushed `2025-01-08`, and is not education-sector software. **It is recorded here for the instrument result only.** Extends `T353`.

## T360 — 🟢 The licence seam in education OSS runs along HOST-PLATFORM LINKAGE, and two independent estates confirmed it in one pass

**Estate 1 — [`eol-uchile`](https://github.com/eol-uchile)** (Educación Online, Universidad de Chile; Open edX operator). **All `109` repositories enumerated.**

| Name contains | `AGPL-3.0` | `MIT` | no grant |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| `xblock` | **`12`** | **`0`** | `5` |
| `theme` | **`0`** | **`12`** | `5` |
| `container` / docker | `0` | `2` | `4` |
| everything else | `9` | `8` | `51` |

🟢 **Zero crossovers across `24` granted repositories.** Totals: **`65` ungranted, `22` MIT, `21` AGPL-3.0, `1` Apache-2.0.**

**Estate 2 — [`mgarlabx/edukors_graph`](https://github.com/mgarlabx/edukors_graph)**, a different ecosystem (Moodle), found the same pass. **Two grants, two depths:** root `LICENSE.md` **MIT** `1,087 B` `625342dc4d3d` with **zero** occurrences of `GPL`; `plugin/edukorsplayer/COPYING.txt` **GPL-3.0** `35,151 B` `e79e9c8a0c85`. The README badge claims *"MIT + GPL-3.0-or-later"*; the boundary is stated **only** in Portuguese at depth 2 (`plugin/plugin.README.md`). 🔴 **The index reports `MIT`** — not wrong about the root, **incomplete about the repository.**

🟢 **The mechanism is one sentence: code that links the host platform inherits the host's copyleft; code that does not is released permissively by the same authors.** Open edX is AGPL → its XBlocks are AGPL. Moodle is GPL → its plugins are GPL. Themes, schemas, validators and Dockerfiles link nothing → MIT.

🔵 **This is `T356` generalised.** `p741` found that *"the `oat-sa` estate is GPL throughout"* concealed one `LGPL-2.1` component; `T360` says **where to look for that component in any estate** rather than discovering it by luck: **at the linkage boundary.** 🟢 **Operationally: take the themes, schemas and deployment layer; reimplement the pedagogy extensions.** Supersedes nothing; wired as `P213`.

It is `91★`, pushed `2026-10-15`.** ⚠️ The owner is now a personal account rather than the Digital Credentials Consortium's, so the North America placement should be re-confirmed with the DCC.

🟡 **A third `422` surfaced as the census ran on to `428` addresses, and it is a FALSE POSITIVE for shelf-defect purposes — recorded because the next pass will run this census and must not mass-rewrite on it.** [`Frederikmh90/RUCAI`](https://github.com/Frederikmh90/RUCAI) answers `422`; the canonical address is [`RUC-Digital-Media-Lab/RUCAI`](https://github.com/RUC-Digital-Media-Lab/RUCAI), byte-identical README (`6,655 B`, sha256₁₂ `45f215f2a5a0`). 🟢 **But `agents/top.md`'s row already cites the organisation address.** The personal address appears only *inside that row's prose*, where `p664` deliberately noted it because the README's own Quick Start clones it.

🔵 **So `P214` needs a precision rule, and this is it: a `422` tells you an address is non-canonical, not that a row is wrong.** Classify the hit by **where the address sits** — a row's link cell is a defect to repair; an address quoted in prose, in a historical note, or in a pattern's worked example is content, and rewriting it would falsify what an earlier pass read. **Of this pass's three `422` hits on shelf addresses, `2` were row defects and `1` was prose.**

> 🟢 **Control, run because this pass's sweep used a lowercased address ledger and a case-sensitive qualifier would have manufactured false `count=0` verdicts.** `repo:` is **case-INSENSITIVE**: `hkuds/deeptutor` and `HKUDS/DeepTutor` both return `count=1`; `thu-maic/openmaic` and `THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC` both return `count=1`. 🟢 **So a lowercased ledger is safe to sweep, and `DaRL-GenAI/instructional_agents` returning `count=0` in *both* casings is a genuine `LIVE-UNINDEXED` state** (raw `200` on README and LICENSE), not a casing artefact.

## T352 — 🔴 A fourth grant-readability state: the terms are asserted, their exact path is named, and the repository holding it does not exist

**`P739-B` established three states** — grant present at a probed path; grant absent from every
probed path (`T302`'s honest negative); grant present in `HEAD` but only at an unconventional path
(`T347`). **`p741` found a fourth, and it is the most dangerous of the four because it reads as
resolved rather than as a gap.**

🟡 **The base already holds the outer finding.** `p718` recorded
[`1EdTech/qti-examples`](https://github.com/1EdTech/qti-examples) (`35★`, `20` forks, pushed
`2026-08-18`) as **unusable — `6` paths, all `404`**. `p741` re-probed it across the full `17`-name
chain, `17 / 17` absent, and then **read the README, which `p718` did not.** It has a
`## License` section and the section is specific:

> *"This project is licensed under the terms of the 1EdTech Consortium Specification Document
> License. See the [LICENSE](https://github.com/1EdTech/qti-central/blob/main/LICENSE) file for
> details."* · `©2026 1EdTech Consortium, Inc. All Rights Reserved.`

🔴 **`1EdTech/qti-central` does not exist.** Three independent channels agree:

| Channel | Probe | Result |
|---|---|---|
| raw | `qti-central` × {`README.md`,`LICENSE`} × {`HEAD`,`main`,`master`} | **`6 / 6` → `404`** |
| search | `gh api -X GET search/repositories -f q=repo:1EdTech/qti-central` | **no count returned at all** |
| enumeration | `org:1edtech qti in:name` | **exactly `1` repository — `qti-examples` itself** |

🔵 **Why the fourth state is worse than the second, and this is the transferable part.** A studio
that probes paths and finds nothing records *"no grant found"* and escalates to the publisher. A
studio that reads this README concludes the terms are **known** — a named licence, a named file —
and proceeds. It has in fact been told the licence is a **Specification Document Licence** (so, per
the base's existing `caliper-spec` record, *not a software grant*) and pointed at a file nobody can
open, in the same block as **`All Rights Reserved`**. **The safe reading is that the QTI example
corpus is not open-source-granted**, which is where `p718` already put it — but now with the reason
attached, so the verdict survives a client challenging it.

**Verdict form for a successor: `GRANT-REFERENCE-DANGLING`. Record the dangling target explicitly,
and never upgrade a *named* licence to a *read* one.** 🟢 **Procedure change, cheap and general:
when a licence chain returns nil, read the README's licence section before filing the nil** — it
either names a path worth probing (`T347`) or names one that does not exist (this finding).

## T353 — 🟢 `apache.org` is reachable, so the operative-text control has a primary reference at last — and the first thing it found was an altered `Apache-2.0`

🟢 **The reachability result first, because it narrows a standing conclusion.**
`P693-I` tested six primary domains (`unesco.org`, `iesalc.unesco.org`, `ipsos.com`,
`teqsa.gov.au`, `eur-lex.europa.eu`, `joinup.ec.europa.eu`), found all six unresolvable, and
concluded that this base *"can read GitHub and web-search summaries; it cannot read the primary
text"*. `p741` fetched **`https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0.txt` → `http=200`,
`11,358 B`.** 🔵 **`P693-I` holds for governments, UN agencies, national regulators and academic
publishers. It does not extend to licence stewards.** Keep the distinction: **licence text is
adjudicable in this session; law and statistics are not.**

🟢 **With a primary reference the control is a different instrument.** `693-G`, `692-G` and `T349`
all compared payloads to **each other** and could say "`7 / 8` agree" but never *which* side was
canonical. Canonical operative text — §1–§9 between `1. Definitions.` and
`END OF TERMS AND CONDITIONS`, whitespace collapsed — is **`8,951` chars at sha256₁₂
`db834674d194`**. Of `7` `Apache-2.0` payloads read this pass, **`6` reproduce it exactly**, across
total file sizes from **`11,264 B` to `13,185 B`** — a **`1,921 B` spread carrying zero terms**,
reproducing `693-G` for a third independent pass at a wider spread than `p739`'s `1,184 B`.

⚠️ **Window note, stated so nobody compares incomparable numbers.** `p741`'s normalisation window
is its own and yields `8,951` for canonical; `p739`'s yielded `8,967`. **The two figures are not
comparable — only within-pass comparison against the fetched canonical is.**

🔴 **The seventh payload is an altered copy, and the direction is now provable.**
[`1EdTech/OpenCASE`](https://github.com/1EdTech/OpenCASE) (`12★`, pushed `2026-11-03`, already on
[`../verticals/solutions.md`](../verticals/solutions.md)) normalises to `8,957` chars at
`0ea735f186e8` — **three edits**, localised by diff and each counted against apache.org's own text:

| Offset | Canonical (occurrences in apache.org text) | OpenCASE (occurrences) |
|--:|---|---|
| `2109` | `intentionally submitted to Licensor` (`1`) | `intentionally submitted to **the** Licensor` (`0`) |
| `2910` | `has been received by Licensor` (`1`) | `has been received by **the** Licensor` (`0`) |
| `5209` | `excluding **those** notices that do not pertain` (`2`) | `excluding **any** notices that do not pertain` (`0`) |

🔵 **So `OpenCASE` is the altered party, not the majority** — the opposite shape from `T349`, where
ADL's variant dropped section labels while preserving every word. ⚠️ **How to treat it:** the first
two edits are grammatical and change nothing; **the third is in §4(d), the NOTICE-attribution
clause**, where `those`→`any` widens what a redistributor may exclude from a NOTICE file. The
practical verdict is unchanged — **it is `Apache-2.0` and it is usable** — but a studio mirroring
licence files under a digest gate will see this payload fail. **Rule, extending `P61`: gate on the
operative digest, and when it fails, diff before you judge.**

## T354 — 🟢 `fork = false` is not evidence of independence; the licence payload's **copyright holder line** is

**Measured, `evidence/maic-copy-detection.2026-11-10-p741.tsv`.** A search for the pass's
highest-starred education agent returned it alongside three lookalikes in the same result set.
🔴 **GitHub reports `fork: false` for every one of them.**

| Repo | Owner | Stars | `fork` | Licence sha256₁₂ | Holder line |
|---|---|--:|---|---|---|
| `THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC` | THU-MAIC | `43,190` | `false` | `ba2525637432` | `Copyright (c) 2026 THU-MAIC` |
| `Tyche-MKR/SmartOpenMAIC` | **Tyche-MKR** | `39` | `false` | **`ba2525637432`** | **`Copyright (c) 2026 THU-MAIC`** |
| `YizukiAme/SpiralMAIC` | **YizukiAme** | `10` | `false` | **`ba2525637432`** | **`Copyright (c) 2026 THU-MAIC`** |
| `THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC-Project` | THU-MAIC | `7` | `false` | `ba2525637432` | `Copyright (c) 2026 THU-MAIC` |
| `THU-MAIC/dsh-openmaic` | THU-MAIC | `122` | `false` | `1c78bffe1e04` | `Copyright (c) 2026 OpenMAIC contributors` |
| `THU-MAIC/MAIC-Vibe` | THU-MAIC | `8` | `false` | `4f726f7a9e40` | *(differs)* |

🟢 **The mechanism, and why the digest alone is not the rule.** An `MIT` payload is `~1,065 B` and
differs between projects *only* in its copyright line, so **a matching digest proves a verbatim
copy including the holder.** Whether that copy is notable is then decided by the **owner** field:
`OpenMAIC-Project` carries the identical payload under the *same* owner — a self-copy, unremarkable
— while `Tyche-MKR` and `YizukiAme` are **third parties shipping THU-MAIC's own copyright notice**.
Meanwhile `dsh-openmaic` and `MAIC-Vibe` are the same owner with **their own** payloads, which is
how an independent sibling looks.

🔵 **Corroboration, and the limit of each signal.** `SmartOpenMAIC`'s `description` field is
byte-identical to `OpenMAIC`'s; `SpiralMAIC` rewrote its description. **Description-matching catches
one of the two; the holder line catches both** — which is why the holder line is the rule and the
description is only corroboration.

**Rule: before filing a row in a cohort, compare the licence-payload digest and the holder line
against the rows already held. `fork: false` means nothing** — a detached copy or a re-initialised
repository reports it exactly as an original does. ⚠️ This is **discovery hygiene, not a licence
finding**: all three are genuinely `MIT` and nothing here says the copies are unlawful. It says
they are **not three projects, they are one.**

`ACTION p739-A` aimed `p741` at named owners, which is good practice and worked. But the pass also
ran the mandated `github trending {industry} AI {year}` leg, which surfaced
[`THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC`](https://github.com/THU-MAIC/OpenMAIC) at `43,190★` as a trending education
agent. `p741` byte-read it (`MIT`, `1,065 B`, `ba2525637432`), confirmed `v1.5.0-rc.1` shipped
**today**, and **drafted a promotion row describing it as "the largest education agent this base
has ever filed".**

🔴 **Every part of that framing was false.** The base has held `OpenMAIC` for roughly twenty
passes: a carried row on `agents/top.md`, **`223` mentions** across the live shelves, and per-pass
star-movement ledgers tracking it from `43,124` at `p724` to `43,147` at `p740`. It is **not** the
largest row — `microsoft/autogen` (`61,761★`) and `HKUDS/DeepTutor` (`57,805★`, re-read this pass,
`+234` since `p740`) are both larger, and `p728` already recorded an `84,290★` refusal.

the live shelves, run *before* writing, not after.** Extended to the whole candidate set:

| Candidate addresses probed | Already on a sell shelf | Novel to sell shelves | Rediscovery rate |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| `27` | **`12`** | `15` | **`44%`** |

🔴 **Why this prices `Gap 247` rather than restating it.** `Gap 247` ("run `make hooks` every
pass") has been recorded as UNMET at `p664`, `p693`, `p739` and now `p741`, each time with the same
environmental cause — every recipe `cd`s into `compose/code/*` and executes code **from the cloned
repository**, which this session refuses. It has read for several passes as a procedural nag.
**It is not.** `gate-promotion-ledger` is precisely the control that rejects a row whose address is
already shelved, and in its absence this pass got within one step of publishing a duplicate of a
`43,000★` holding. **The missing gate is worth one such defect per pass at the observed
rediscovery rate.** 🔵 **Interim remedy a successor can run with no permissions at all, and it cost
`p741` one command:**
`grep -rF "{owner}/{repo}" --include=*.md . | grep -v '^./archive/'` **before writing any row.**
Zero mentions means novel; a hit on `agents/top.md`, `repos/foundations.md` or
`verticals/solutions.md` means **do not file a row — file a re-verification instead.**

## T356 — 🟢 "The `oat-sa` estate is `GPL`/`LGPL` throughout" is true and hides the one component that matters: the `LGPL-2.1` seam, now named

🟡 **The base already knows the headline.** Pass 222 (`2026-10-15`) recorded an organisation-wide

which is the whole content of `P211`. ⚠️ **`GPL-2.0-only` has no `or-later` clause**, so Pass 222's
Moodle-GPLv3 incompatibility stands untouched: **the seam is for integration, never for
redistribution in one artefact.**

# 🆕 Trends new at `p740` (researched 2026-11-10) — `T344`–`T351`

**Added above `p739`'s `T337`–`T343`.** 🔴 **Six of the eight are instrument findings, and three of
them say the same thing: `p739` was right that the bytes are the verdict, and wrong to assume that
reading the bytes is easy.** A keyword classifier applied to a licence payload in the obvious order
misfiles `GPL-3.0` as `AGPL-3.0`, misfiles `MPL-2.0` as `GPL-3.0`, and rejects a valid `Apache-2.0`
grant. All three were caught on this pass against **`36` byte-read payloads (`36 / 36`
classified)**, and all three have fixes that are one line of ordering each.

## T344 — 🔴 A keyword classifier cannot tell `GPL-3.0` from `AGPL-3.0`, because `GPL-3.0` names the Affero licence in its own section 13

`GPL-3.0`'s section 13 is **titled** *"Use with the GNU Affero General Public License"* and the
string `Affero` occurs **`3` times** in a plain `GPL-3.0` payload. So the natural test —
`grep -i "GNU AFFERO GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE"` — **matches `GPL-3.0`**, and every `GPL-3.0`
repository on the pass was initially filed as `AGPL-3.0`.

🟢 **The discriminator that works is `AGPL-3.0`'s own section 13 heading, `Remote Network
Interaction`**, which has no counterpart in `GPL-3.0`. Measured on `7` copyleft payloads this pass,
`7 / 7` decided:

| Repo | Licence path | `Remote Network Interaction` | Verdict | Payload | sha256₁₂ |
|---|---|:-:|---|--:|---|
| [openstax/openstax-cms](https://github.com/openstax/openstax-cms) | `LICENSE` | **1** | **AGPL-3.0** | `34,541 B` | `6179a3052bab` |
| [openstax/exercises](https://github.com/openstax/exercises) | `GNU-AGPL-3.0` | **1** | **AGPL-3.0** | `34,519 B` | `91b65277959e` |
| [openedx/edx-platform](https://github.com/openedx/edx-platform) | `LICENSE` | **1** | **AGPL-3.0** | `35,136 B` | `e12d78569742` |
| [eol-uchile/eol-conditional-xblock](https://github.com/eol-uchile/eol-conditional-xblock) | `LICENSE` | **1** | **AGPL-3.0** | `34,523 B` | `8486a10c4393` |
| [EsupPortail/Esup-Pod](https://github.com/EsupPortail/Esup-Pod) | `COPYING` | **0** | 🟢 **GPL-3.0** | `35,149 B` | `3972dc9744f6` |
| [bycs-lp/moodle-block_ai_control](https://github.com/bycs-lp/moodle-block_ai_control) | `LICENSE` | **0** | 🟢 **GPL-3.0** | `35,149 B` | `3972dc9744f6` |
| [bycs-lp/moodle-tiny_ai](https://github.com/bycs-lp/moodle-tiny_ai) | `LICENSE.md` | **0** | 🟢 **GPL-3.0** | `35,178 B` | `ccb349b4132e` |

🔵 **Why this is the most consequential instrument finding this base has recorded.** The
`GPL-3.0` / `AGPL-3.0` line is the line that decides whether a studio may **host a modified
instance for a client without publishing its source**. Filing `GPL-3.0` as `AGPL-3.0` kills a
sellable engagement on a false premise; the reverse exposes the client. Two of this pass's three
`GPL-3.0` repositories — **a state ministry's Moodle plugins** — would have been filed `AGPL-3.0`.
🟢 **It also independently confirms `p739`'s AGPL call on `eol-uchile`:** that one really does
carry `Remote Network Interaction`.

⚠️ **One index disagreement falls out of it.** `EsupPortail/Esup-Pod` **indexes `LGPL-3.0`**; its
`COPYING` is `GPL-3.0`, byte-identical (`3972dc9744f6`) to a Bavarian ministry's plugin. `LGPL`
permits proprietary linking and `GPL` does not, so this is the third index error in two passes and
the second in the permissive direction.

## T345 — 🔴 `MPL-2.0` names the GNU GPL in its own definitions, so the same ordering misfiles it as `GPL-3.0`

`MPL-2.0` defines a *"Secondary License"* as **"the GNU General Public License, Version 2.0, the
GNU Lesser General Public License, Version 2.1, the GNU Affero General Public License, Version
3.0, or any later versions"**, and repeats the family in Exhibit B. The string
`GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE` is therefore **present in every `MPL-2.0` payload**.

Measured on `4` fresh `edanalytics` payloads, all four initially misfiled as `GPL-3.0`:

| Repo | Licence path | Payload | sha256₁₂ | Verdict |
|---|---|--:|---|---|
| [edanalytics/edu_wh](https://github.com/edanalytics/edu_wh) | `LICENSE.md` | `16,727 B` | `d8d2562a7cb6` | **MPL-2.0** |
| [edanalytics/edu_edfi_source](https://github.com/edanalytics/edu_edfi_source) | `LICENSE.md` | `16,727 B` | `d8d2562a7cb6` | **MPL-2.0** |
| [edanalytics/edu_ext_oneroster](https://github.com/edanalytics/edu_ext_oneroster) | `LICENSE.md` | `16,727 B` | `d8d2562a7cb6` | **MPL-2.0** |
| [edanalytics/startingblocks_oss](https://github.com/edanalytics/startingblocks_oss) | `LICENSE` | `16,725 B` | `1f256ecad192` | **MPL-2.0** |

🟢 **`T344` and `T345` are one rule, and it is one line of code: order the classifier by
specificity, not by alphabet.** Test `Mozilla Public License` and `released into the public
domain` **before** the GPL family; inside the GPL family, test `Remote Network Interaction`
before the title line; test the title line before any body text. Under that order all `21`
payloads on this pass classify correctly. 🔵 **The index was right about all four of these and the
naive payload read was wrong — which is the mirror image of `p739`'s `T338`.** The lesson is not
"trust the index" or "trust the bytes": it is **read the bytes with a classifier that knows the
licences quote each other.**

## T346 — 🟢 Copyleft payload size does not merely fail to identify the licence; it points the wrong way

| Family | Payloads this pass | Range |
|---|--:|---|
| **AGPL-3.0** | `4` | `34,519` – `35,136 B` |
| **GPL-3.0** | `3` | `35,149` – `35,178 B` |

🔴 **Every `GPL-3.0` payload measured is larger than every `AGPL-3.0` payload measured** — and the
more permissive of the pair is the bigger file. `p739`'s `693-G` established that `Apache-2.0`
payload size carries no information about the terms. **`T346` strengthens that from "uninformative"
to "actively misleading": a reviewer using size as a sanity check on a copyleft call will be
confirmed in the wrong answer.** Size is not a weak signal here. It is an inverted one.

## T347 — 🟢 A grant can be present in `HEAD` and absent from every licence path, and this pass found three distinct hiding places

`p739`'s `T341` found a repository whose asserted `GPL-3.0` grant existed only inside a release
archive, and concluded that "a studio cloning `HEAD` receives no licence file". **That is one
branch of three.** p740 probed `16` licence paths per repository and found grants living in three
other places:

| Hiding place | Case | What `16` probed paths return | Where the grant actually is |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Per-file headers** | [bycs-lp/moodle-local_ai_manager](https://github.com/bycs-lp/moodle-local_ai_manager) (`30★`), [moodle-block_ai_chat](https://github.com/bycs-lp/moodle-block_ai_chat) (`16★`), [moodle-quizaccess_ai](https://github.com/bycs-lp/moodle-quizaccess_ai) (`1★`) | **`16 / 16` → `404`**, index `None` | `version.php`, `lib.php`, `classes/manager.php` each carry *"Moodle is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify it under the terms of the GNU General Public License … either version 3 of the License, or (at your option) any later version"* — **`3 / 3` files checked, `3 / 3` carry it** |
| **Non-standard filename** | [openstax/fine_print](https://github.com/openstax/fine_print) (`40★`) | `LICENSE`, `LICENSE.txt`, `LICENSE.md`, `license.txt` all `404` | **`MIT-LICENSE`** — the Rails/RubyGems convention — `1,055 B`, sha256₁₂ `0a9ed2a2ba71`, **MIT**. The index said MIT and was right. |
| **A `COPYRIGHT` file named in the README** | [openstax/exercises](https://github.com/openstax/exercises) (`13★`, pushed **2026-11-10**) | `LICENSE`, `LICENSE.txt`, `LICENSE.md`, `COPYING` all `404` | an HTML comment at the top of `README.md` points to `COPYRIGHT` (`1,186 B`), which points to a file named **`GNU-AGPL-3.0`** (`34,519 B`, `91b65277959e`) |

🟢 **So `T341` gets its missing branches, and the rule becomes decidable:** *no licence file* is
**not** *no grant*. Before filing "no grant found", check (1) the source-file headers of the
ecosystem the repository belongs to — Moodle, WordPress and Drupal plugins all mandate one —
(2) `MIT-LICENSE` and the other ecosystem-conventional filenames, and (3) whatever the README
points at. ⚠️ **Only after all three does `T302`'s "no grant found" verdict apply.** On this pass
that reclassified **`3` repositories from "unbuildable" to `GPL-3.0`-or-later** and **`1` from
"unbuildable" to MIT** — four rows that a path-only probe would have discarded.

## T348 — 🔴 One repository, three grants, and neither the index nor a single-file byte read can express it

[`openstax/exercises`](https://github.com/openstax/exercises) — Rice University, pushed
**2026-11-10** — splits its grant three ways in the `COPYRIGHT` file:

1. **Programmatic source** → `AGPL-3.0`-or-later;
2. **Vendored components** (Rails, jQuery, Devise) → `MIT/X11`, *"All unmodified files from these
   and other sources retain their original copyright and license notices"*;
3. 🔴 **Everything non-programmatic** — *"logos, images, videos, marketing materials, and text
   copy"* — **`Copyright Rice University, All Rights Reserved"`**, and *"derivations … may not use
   these materials"*.

🔵 **For a studio this is the single most expensive shape a grant can take**, because the part that
is All-Rights-Reserved is the part a client sees. The exercise *content* a buyer assumes is open is
the asset explicitly withheld. The index reports one SPDX string per repository and cannot say
this; a byte read of one file says only `AGPL-3.0`. ⚠️ **File this shape, not just the licence: for
any content-bearing repository, read the `COPYRIGHT`/`NOTICE` text for an asset carve-out before
the SOW is signed.** Extends `p737`'s `T327` (permissive components over a copyleft core) with its
commercial inverse: **copyleft code over proprietary content.**

## T349 — 🔴 The `Apache-2.0` operative-text digest is not universal, and the variant that breaks it is the US Department of Defense's

`p739`'s `693-G` normalised three `Apache-2.0` payloads spanning `1,184 B` to one operative digest
and concluded the byte count is noise. p740 re-ran the control on **`8` fresh payloads** under its
own normalisation (strip from `APPENDIX`, collapse whitespace) and got **`7 / 8` identical at
`9,129` chars, digest sha256₁₂ `59d8f0ba87ad` — and one outlier**:

| Repo | Raw | `APPENDIX` | Operative chars | Operative sha256₁₂ |
|---|--:|:-:|--:|---|
| [adlnet/xapi-profiles](https://github.com/adlnet/xapi-profiles) | `11,357 B` | yes | `9,129` | `59d8f0ba87ad` |
| [adlnet/CATAPULT](https://github.com/adlnet/CATAPULT) | `11,358 B` | yes | `9,129` | `59d8f0ba87ad` |
| [adlnet/xapi-ontology](https://github.com/adlnet/xapi-ontology) | `11,525 B` | yes | `9,129` | `59d8f0ba87ad` |
| [edanalytics/earthmover](https://github.com/edanalytics/earthmover) | `11,349 B` | yes | `9,129` | `59d8f0ba87ad` |
| [EsupPortail/esup-signature](https://github.com/EsupPortail/esup-signature) | `11,361 B` | yes | `9,129` | `59d8f0ba87ad` |
| [adlnet/xapi-authored-profiles](https://github.com/adlnet/xapi-authored-profiles) | `11,357 B` | yes | `9,129` | `59d8f0ba87ad` |
| [adlnet/ADL_LRS](https://github.com/adlnet/ADL_LRS) | `11,357 B` | yes | `9,129` | `59d8f0ba87ad` |
| 🔴 [adlnet/xAPIWrapper](https://github.com/adlnet/xAPIWrapper) | `10,273 B` | yes | **`9,113`** | **`da0ea9556182`** |

🟢 **The `16`-character difference was localised by diff, and it is in the one section that binds a
redistributor.** `xAPIWrapper`'s copy **drops the `(a)`, `(b)`, `(c)`, `(d)` labels from section 4's
four redistribution conditions** — give a copy of the Licence, mark modified files, retain the
notices, reproduce `NOTICE`. **The conditions survive as prose; only the enumeration is gone.**

🔵 **So the verdict stands and the gate fails.** The grant is `Apache-2.0` and a studio's
obligations are unchanged — but a licence gate that compares the operative digest against a single
known-good value **rejects a valid `Apache-2.0` grant from the publisher of the xAPI specification
itself.** ⚠️ **Consequence for `P61`'s lockfile and any digest gate: carry an allowlist of
known-good operative digests, or compare clause presence rather than a hash.** `693-G` was true of
its four payloads and does not generalise to eight. 🟢 **One further confirmation falls out of the
larger sample:** `adlnet/ADL_LRS` and `adlnet/xapi-authored-profiles` have *different raw digests*
(`58d1e17ffe51` and `b40930bbcf80`) at the *same* `11,357 B` and *identical* operative text — the
whole difference is in the filled-in `APPENDIX` boilerplate. **Raw digest varies for reasons that
carry no legal weight; the operative digest is the only comparison worth making, and even it needs
an allowlist.**

## T350 — 🟢 France has bound the *tool* rather than the *use*, and it is the first instrument in this base that reaches procurement

Every EMEA instrument this base has filed — the AI Act's Annex III tier at `2027-12-02`, the
transparency and literacy duties live since `2025`, the national designation layer — regulates
**how an institution uses** an AI system. **France's Interoperability Framework for Digital
Services for Education, adopted January 2026, regulates what an institution may buy.** Per
1EdTech's announcement (vendor source, so read as secondary), it requires **public middle and high
schools to use digital tools and services that comply with technical requirements for security,
interoperability and responsible digital technology set by the Minister**, and the framework
favours **open standards**.

🟢 **Why this is a different kind of opportunity from everything else on the EMEA shelf.** An
Annex III obligation is a reason for a client to buy *governance*. A procurement framework is a
reason for a client to buy *conformance* — and conformance is testable, which means it is
deliverable on a fixed price with an acceptance criterion. It also travels: 1EdTech's own reading is
that a French vendor conforming to the framework can **sell into other markets using the same
standards**, which makes the same conformance work reusable across the region.

🔵 **The demand context sharpens it, and it is a counter-signal to `p738`'s `T336`.** The OECD's
*Digital Education Outlook 2026* puts teacher agreement that AI helps with lesson plans at
**`18 %` in France — the lowest in its set — against `91 %` in Viet Nam**, the highest; and a
German survey of **over `23,000` higher-education students** finds **`94 %` used AI in 2025,
`65 %` daily or weekly**. ⚠️ **So France is simultaneously the EMEA market with the most binding
procurement obligation and the least convinced teaching workforce.** A pitch built on "AI helps
teachers" is aimed at the `18 %`. A pitch built on "this is the conformant, sovereign,
French-hosted way to run it" is aimed at the obligation — and the obligation does not need
convincing. See `P207` and the EMEA section of `intel/market.md`.
